_**Flightplan**_ is a 2005 [mystery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mystery_film "Mystery film")[psychological thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychological_thriller "Psychological thriller") film directed by [Robert Schwentke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Schwentke "Robert Schwentke") from a screenplay written by [Peter A. Dowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_A._Dowling "Peter A. Dowling") and [Billy Ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Ray_(screenwriter) "Billy Ray (screenwriter)"). It stars [Jodie Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster "Jodie Foster") as Kyle Pratt, a recently widowed American aircraft engineer living in [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin"), who flies back to the United States with her daughter and her husband's body. She loses her daughter during the flight and must struggle to find her while proving her sanity at the same time.[[N 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-4) It also features [Peter Sarsgaard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Sarsgaard "Peter Sarsgaard"), [Erika Christensen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erika_Christensen "Erika Christensen"), [Kate Beahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Beahan "Kate Beahan"), [Greta Scacchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Scacchi "Greta Scacchi"), [Sean Bean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Bean "Sean Bean"), and [Matt Bomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Bomer "Matt Bomer") in his film debut.

Released theatrically by [Buena Vista Pictures Distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buena_Vista_Pictures_Distribution "Buena Vista Pictures Distribution") on September 23, 2005, in the United States and on October 20, 2005, in Germany, the film received mixed reviews from critics, who praised the direction, performances of the cast (particularly Foster's), and the thriller elements of the film but criticized the screenplay. It was also a major commercial success, grossing over $223 million worldwide on a $55 million budget, and received two nominations at the [32nd Saturn Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/32nd_Saturn_Awards "32nd Saturn Awards"); [Best Action or Adventure Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_Award_for_Best_Action_or_Adventure_Film "Saturn Award for Best Action or Adventure Film"), and [Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_Award_for_Best_Actress "Saturn Award for Best Actress") (for Foster).

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flightplan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Recently widowed Berlin-based American aviation engineer Kyle Pratt is taking her husband David's body back to the United States. Traveling with their six-year-old daughter Julia, they board a new double-decker aircraft Kyle helped design.

Awakening from a nap, Kyle finds Julia is gone, and no one recalls seeing her. Flight attendant Stephanie tells her there is no record of her daughter boarding the flight, and Julia's boarding pass and backpack are missing. At a panicked Kyle's insistence, Captain Marcus Rich conducts a search, while [sky marshal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_marshal "Sky marshal") Gene Carson monitors her. Kyle accuses two [Arab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab "Arab") passengers of stalking her daughter the night before, resulting in a fight and her being handcuffed.

Kyle reveals that her husband died in an apparent fall from the roof of a building, though she suspects it was not a suicide. Captain Rich receives a message from a Berlin hospital that Julia died with her father, and is convinced that Kyle, unhinged by her husband's and daughter's deaths, imagined bringing her on board. The increasingly erratic Kyle is confined to her seat, where a therapist, Lisa, consoles her. Kyle doubts her own sanity until she notices the heart Julia drew in the condensation on the window next to her seat.

Kyle asks to use the bathroom, where she climbs into the overhead crawl space, sabotaging the aircraft's electronics. In the ensuing chaos, she rides a [dumbwaiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dumbwaiter "Dumbwaiter") to the lower freight deck and unlocks David's casket, suspecting Julia to be inside, but finds only her husband's body. Carson escorts Kyle to her seat in handcuffs, and explains the flight is making an emergency stopover at [Goose Bay Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CFB_Goose_Bay "CFB Goose Bay") in [Labrador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labrador "Labrador"), where she will be taken into custody.

Kyle pleads with Carson to search the hold. He sneaks down to the freight deck, removing two explosives and a detonator concealed in David's casket, and planting the explosives in the [avionics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avionics "Avionics") section. It is revealed that Carson, Stephanie, and the Berlin mortuary director have conspired to hijack the aircraft for a $50 million ransom and frame Kyle; they abducted Julia to coerce Kyle into unlocking the casket. Carson also falsely claims to Captain Rich that Kyle is threatening to bomb the aircraft unless the ransom is wired to a bank account and a [G3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulfstream_III "Gulfstream III") aircraft is readied upon landing. He then plans to detonate the explosives, killing Julia, and leaving Kyle dead with the detonator in her hand.

Landing in Newfoundland, the airliner is surrounded by [FBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FBI "FBI") agents as the passengers exit the aircraft. Kyle confronts Captain Rich, who angrily declares the ransom has been paid. Realizing that Carson is the perpetrator, she quickly assumes the role of hijacker, commanding Carson to remain aboard and the crew to disembark.

Once the plane's door closes, Kyle knocks Carson out with a fire extinguisher, handcuffs him to a rail, and takes the detonator from his pocket. He quickly regains consciousness, frees himself and pursues Kyle, who locks herself in the cockpit. She draws Carson away by throwing a binder out a hatch door to the upper level as a ruse so she can escape. After an altercation with Kyle, a guilt-ridden Stephanie flees the airliner.

Kyle finds the unconscious Julia, but Carson arrives, revealing that he murdered David to smuggle the explosives inside his casket and gagged and dumped Julia into the food bin, believing that neither the passengers nor the crew would notice. Kyle escapes with Julia into the aircraft's non-combustible hold as Carson shoots at her. She detonates the explosives, killing him and damaging the landing gear, but she and Julia emerge unscathed as everyone realizes she had been telling the truth all along.

The next morning, in the passenger waiting section of the airport, Captain Rich apologizes to a seated Kyle holding Julia in her arms as Stephanie is led away by FBI agents. One agent approaches to inform them that the Berlin mortuary director has also been arrested, adding that they are tracking down another accomplice who erased Julia's record from the flight manifest.

Kyle silently redeems herself by carrying Julia through the crowd of passengers. As one of the Arab passengers assists Kyle in loading her luggage onto a waiting van, Julia awakens and sleepily asks "Are we there yet?" as they drive away.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flightplan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flightplan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Development")]

The film draws heavily on [Alfred Hitchcock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Hitchcock "Alfred Hitchcock")'s _[The Lady Vanishes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lady\_Vanishes "The Lady Vanishes")_, in which one passenger goes missing on board a train and only the main character remembers her, especially in the scene where Kyle discovers the heart drawn by her daughter on the plane window. The similarities have led to _Flightplan_ being called a “[remake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remake "Remake")” of Hitchcock’s film.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-5)[Peter A. Dowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_A._Dowling "Peter A. Dowling") claims having had the idea for _Flightplan_ in 1999 on a phone conversation with a friend. His original pitch for producer [Brian Grazer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Grazer "Brian Grazer") involved a man who worked on airport security doing a business trip from the United States to Hong Kong, and during the flight his son went missing. A few years later, [Billy Ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Ray_(screenwriter) "Billy Ray (screenwriter)") took over the script, taking out the terrorists from the story and putting more emphasis on the protagonist, who became a female as Grazer thought it would be a good role for [Jodie Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster "Jodie Foster"). The story then focused on the main character regaining her psyche, and added the post-[September 11 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks "September 11 attacks") tension and paranoia. There was also an attempt to hide the identity of the villain by showcasing the different characters on the plane. Both Dowling and Ray were allowed to visit the insides of a [Boeing 747](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_747 "Boeing 747") at the [Los Angeles International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_International_Airport "Los Angeles International Airport") to develop the limited space set for the story.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-inflight-6)

### Casting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flightplan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Casting")]

Robert Schwentke said that to make _Flightplan_ as realistic as possible, he wanted naturalistic, subdued performances. One example was [Peter Sarsgaard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Sarsgaard "Peter Sarsgaard"), whom he described as an actor "who can all of a sudden become a snake uncoiling". First-time actress Marlene Lawston was cast as Foster's character's daughter Julia. [Sean Bean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Bean "Sean Bean") was cast to subvert his [typecasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typecasting "Typecasting") as a villain and mislead audiences into thinking he was part of the villainous plot.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-inflight-6) Schwentke also picked each of the 300 passengers through auditions.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-cabin-7)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flightplan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Filming")]

Schwentke described _Flightplan_ as a "slow boiling" thriller, where the opening is different from the faster ending parts. The director added that sound was used to put audiences "off-kilter".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-inflight-6)

The art direction team had to build all the interiors and the cockpit of the fictional Elgin E-474 from scratch, basing both the interior design and layout on the [Airbus A380](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbus_A380 "Airbus A380"), with its aircraft's classification number similar to the 747. The amount of dead space within the cabin, cargo and [avionic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avionics "Avionics") areas of the E-474 did not reflect the actual amount of dead space within any aircraft. [BE Aerospace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BE_Aerospace "BE Aerospace") provided various objects to "stage the scene"; "many of the interior sets used real aircraft components such as seats and galleys."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-Beck-8)

To allow for varied camera angles, the set had many tracks for the [camera dolly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camera_dolly "Camera dolly") to move, and both the walls and the ceiling were built on hinges so they could easily be swung open for shooting. The design and colors tried to invoke the mood for each scene. For instance, a white room for "eerie, clinical, cold" moments, lower ceilings for claustrophobia, and wide open spaces to give no clues to the audience.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-cabin-7) Most exterior scenes of the E-474 involve a model one-tenth of the aircraft's actual size, with the images being subsequently enhanced through [computer-generated imagery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-generated_imagery "Computer-generated imagery"). The explosion in the nose involved both life sized and scaled pieces of scenery. A one-half scale set of the avionics area was constructed to make the explosion and fireball look bigger.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-inflight-6)

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flightplan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Music")]

The [score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_score "Film score") for _Flightplan_ was released September 20, 2005, on [Hollywood Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Records "Hollywood Records"). The music was composed and conducted by [James Horner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Horner "James Horner") and performed by the [Hollywood Studio Symphony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Studio_Symphony "Hollywood Studio Symphony"), and the disc contains eight tracks. Horner stated that film's score tried to mix the sound effects with "the emotion and drive of the music", and the instruments were picked to match the "feelings of panic" Kyle goes through. These included [Gamelan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamelan "Gamelan") instruments, [prepared piano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prepared_piano "Prepared piano"), and string arrangements. No [brass instruments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brass_instrument "Brass instrument") are used in the soundtrack.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-inflight-6)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flightplan&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flightplan&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Box office")]

_Flightplan_ opened at [number one at the US and Canadian box office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_2005_box_office_number-one_films_in_the_United_States "List of 2005 box office number-one films in the United States"), grossing $24.6 million in its opening weekend. It grossed $89.7 million in the United States and Canada, and $133.7 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $223.4 million.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-mojo-3) In the week ending October 23, 2005, it opened at number one in Germany with an opening weekend gross of $3.8 million as well as opening at number one in seven other countries including Brazil and Sweden.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-9)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-10) It also grossed $79,270,000 on DVD rentals.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flightplan&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Critical response")]

On [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") the film has an approval rating of 37% based on 175 reviews, with an average rating of 5.3/10. The site's critics consensus states: "The actors are all on key here, but as the movie progresses, tension deflates as the far-fetched plot kicks in."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-11) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), it has a weighted average score of 53 out of 100 rating, based on 33 critics, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-12) Audiences surveyed by [CinemaScore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CinemaScore "CinemaScore") gave the film an average grade B+ on an A+ to F scale.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-13)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-14)

Film historian [Leonard Maltin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard_Maltin "Leonard Maltin") in _Leonard Maltin's 2012 Movie Guide_ (2011) described _Flightplan_ as "suspenseful at first, this thriller becomes remote and un-involving; by the climax, it's just plain ridiculous."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-15)

[Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") gave it 3 and a half out of 4 stars, praising its "airtight plot" and the acting performances.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-16) Other reviewers including _[The Christian Science Monitor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Christian\_Science\_Monitor "The Christian Science Monitor")_ criticised "plotholes the size of an [Airbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbus "Airbus") in the script".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-17)

Aviation film historian Simon D. Beck in _The Aircraft-Spotter's Film and Television Companion_ (2016) noted that _Flightplan_ was careful in setting the scene. "The aircraft is a fictional mammoth airliner called the 'E-474', a double-deck [jumbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jumbo_jet "Jumbo jet") modeled strongly after the [Airbus A-380](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbus_A-380 "Airbus A-380"), the large size being suitable for the missing-person plot of the film."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-Beck-8)

## Controversy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flightplan&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Controversy")]

The [Association of Professional Flight Attendants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_Professional_Flight_Attendants "Association of Professional Flight Attendants") called for an official [boycott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boycott "Boycott") of the film, which they said depicts [flight attendants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_attendant "Flight attendant") as rude and [unsympathetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apathy "Apathy") towards a distressed passenger; the flight attendants and the pilot viewed Foster's character as [delusional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delusional "Delusional") and barely attempted to help her, in addition to one flight attendant revealed to be an [accomplice to terrorists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accomplice "Accomplice") (as part of a strategy to [extort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extort "Extort") a ransom from the airline). As such, the group postulated that the film could spread [distrust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distrust "Distrust") of their members among airline passengers.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-today-18)

Tommie Hutto-Blake, president of the Association of Professional Flight Attendants, stated, "Should there be another [9/11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9/11 "9/11"), it would be critical for the [cabin crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabin_crew "Cabin crew") to have the support of their passengers, not the distrust that this movie may engender... Our fellow crew members who perished in the line of [duty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duty "Duty") deserve more respect".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-today-18) Two other trade organizations, the Association of Flight Attendants and Transport Workers Union Local 556, also called for a boycott.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_note-today-18)

## Notes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flightplan&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Notes")]

1.   [↑](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan#cite_ref-4)The plot's basic premise (albeit with a very different denouement) is similar to a 1955 episode of _[Alfred Hitchcock Presents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred\_Hitchcock\_Presents "Alfred Hitchcock Presents")_ titled "[Into Thin Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Into_Thin_Air_(Alfred_Hitchcock_Presents_episode) "Into Thin Air (Alfred Hitchcock Presents episode)")", as well as [Hitchcock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Hitchcock "Alfred Hitchcock")'s 1938 film _[The Lady Vanishes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lady\_Vanishes\_(1938\_film) "The Lady Vanishes (1938 film)")_. It is also reminiscent of the 1950 British film _[So Long at the Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So\_Long\_at\_the\_Fair "So Long at the Fair")_.

# The Fifth Estate

[Drama](https://www.rogerebert.com/genre/drama)

[Christy Lemire](https://www.rogerebert.com/contributors/christy-lemire)

 October 18, 2013 

 4 min read 

![Image 5](https://www.rogerebert.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/The-Fifth-Estate.jpg)

"The Fifth Estate"

For a movie about a larger-than-life personality who shook up the world with his brazenness—and since has had to seek political asylum because of it—”The Fifth Estate” feels unfortunately small and safe.

Director [Bill Condon](https://www.rogerebert.com/cast-and-crew/bill-condon) tells the story of WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange in a way that seems insular and familiar. It is a tried-and-true tale of rise and fall—of a self-made political and cultural phenomenon whose ambitions are tidily explained away through pop psychology.

The man who has dared to post millions of classified documents online—ones which could potentially compromise both national security and individuals’ well-being—certainly must be more than a self-aggrandizing troublemaker. (Although the 42-year-old Australian does continue to issue insistent missives from the Ecuadorian embassy in London, which has protected him for over a year now.)

In the hands of a supremely creepy [Benedict Cumberbatch](https://www.rogerebert.com/cast-and-crew/benedict-cumberbatch), it’s easy to imagine how this persuasive, commanding force has mystified the world at large and entranced a few key followers in particular. He’s off-putting yet beguiling, odd but elegant. He constantly spouts the need for transparency but lies to everyone around him. But despite Cumberbatch’s formidable presence, Assange remains elusive, a white-haired ghost—more of an idea than a fully fleshed-out and complicated man.

Maybe that’s the point of Josh Singer’s script, based on a couple of books: “Inside WikiLeaks: My Time With Julian Assange at the World’s Most Dangerous Website” by Daniel Domscheit-Berg and “WikiLeaks: Inside Julian Assange’s War on Secrecy” by [David Leigh](https://www.rogerebert.com/cast-and-crew/david-leigh) and [Luke Harding](https://www.rogerebert.com/cast-and-crew/luke-harding). But it does make it hard to get a grasp on him as a viewer, which is problematic given that he’s the engine that drives the film’s action.

About that action: Sitting at a laptop typing away furiously isn’t the most inherently cinematic pursuit. (Trust me, I’m doing it right now, you wouldn’t want to see it.) [David Fincher](https://www.rogerebert.com/cast-and-crew/david-fincher) solved that puzzle in “[The Social Network](https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/the-social-network-2010)” by creating a vivid, thrilling sense of place and through Aaron Sorkin’s sharp, lively dialogue. Condon has found clever, emotionally honest avenues into real-life figures in his previous films “[Gods and Monsters](https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/gods-and-monsters-1998)” and “[Kinsey](https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/kinsey-2004)” and shown a flair for the theatrical with “Dreamgirls” and the two-part “Twilight” finale; here, he tries to dramatize his characters’ interior lives through a motif that’s overly simplistic and rather gimmicky.

He envisions a giant office filled with multiple desks where multiple Assanges hammer away, exposing the truth. (Assange repeatedly informs skeptics and fans alike that WikiLeaks “has thousands of volunteers,” when actually it’s just him and his hardworking second-in-command, Berg, played by [Daniel Brühl](https://www.rogerebert.com/cast-and-crew/daniel-br%C3%BChl).) This sprawling room also serves as the imaginary location of the submission platform, where whistle-blowers could offer up secrets while maintaining anonymity through a complex encryption system. When it all begins to fall apart and the pressure becomes too much, “The Fifth Estate” depicts Berg smashing all that imaginary office furniture in a way that looks like a tantrum and comes off as more of a laughable moment than a startling one.

Condon is also too reliant on montages to cram in a ton of information while simultaneously providing a sense of movement as Assange and Berg hop from one major European city to the next collecting secret information. To the tune of Carter Burwell’s thumping techno score to go with the frequently sleek architecture, this technique often makes “The Fifth Estate” feel like a glossy travelogue: Look, they’re in Brussels! Now they’re in Stockholm! Ooh, Reykjavik looks pretty!

The film begins in October 2010—which seems like a lifetime ago in the Internet age—with The New York Times, The Guardian and Der Spiegel simultaneously publishing WikiLeaks’ Iraq War Logs: 400,000 classified U.S. military documents about the war in Iraq. Editors in all three cities anguish over pressing the button and blasting the story to the world. The moment also provides a flashback to when the German technology expert Berg first met Assange in 2007, quickly fell under his spell and became the fledgling website’s first volunteer. Berg is intended as our everyman conduit but compared to the shiny Assange, he’s rather dull; Brühl registers far more effectively as the precise and demanding racecar driver Niki Lauda in Ron Howard’s “Rush.”

From there, “The Fifth Estate” follows Assange’s rise to celebrity as WikiLeaks reveals more and more secret and damning information. But aside from a few scenes involving [Stanley Tucci](https://www.rogerebert.com/cast-and-crew/stanley-tucci), [Laura Linney](https://www.rogerebert.com/cast-and-crew/laura-linney) and [Anthony Mackie](https://www.rogerebert.com/cast-and-crew/anthony-mackie) as U.S. government officials wringing their hands and shuffling papers—truly, these supporting roles are a huge waste of three great actors—we don’t get much of a sense of the global repercussions of the documents’ disclosure. A subplot involving a threat to a longtime asset of Linney’s character in Libya (Alexander Siddig, also underused) feels underexplored; it’s a blip, when in truth his situation is emblematic of the huge moral quandary that arises repeatedly when WikiLeaks chooses to expose every classified word.

“The Fifth Estate” seems more interested in contributing to a cult of personality, rather than cultivating a serious debate.

Kenyan actor

**Peter King Nzioki Mwania** (born 25 May 1978), popularly known as **Peter King**, is a Kenyan actor.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2) He is best known for his roles in the films _[The Constant Gardener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Constant\_Gardener\_(film) "The Constant Gardener (film)")_, _[The Fifth Estate](link_4)_ and _[Sense8](link_5)_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Nzioki&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Nzioki was born on 25 May 1978 in [Nairobi, Kenya](link_6). His father Michael David Mwania, served in the [Kenyan Army](link_7) and his mother worked at the military hospital. At the age of six, he joined church productions at the [Lang’ata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lang [link_8]'ata "Lang'ata") Barracks. He completed his education from Lang’ata High School in [Nairobi](link_6).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-kenyabuzz-3)

He is married to fellow actress Tess King.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-4)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Nzioki&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

He made his acting debut in 2000 at the [Kenya](link_3) National Theatre for three years under the guidance of Joab Kanuka. In theater, he played 'Iago' in the Phoenix Players production of the [Shakespeare](link_9) tragedy _[Othello](link_10)_. In 2005, he made his film debut with a minor role in _[The Constant Gardener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Constant\_Gardener\_(film) "The Constant Gardener (film)")_ directed by [Fernando Meirelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Meirelles "Fernando Meirelles").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-kenyabuzz-3) In the same year, he appeared as 'Barman' in the television movie _[Transit](link_11)_. In 2016, he appeared in the thriller film _[The CEO](link_12)_ where he played the role of 'Jomo'. The film had its premier 10 July 2016, at the Eko Hotels & Suites, [Victoria Island, Lagos](link_13)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-5) and later received critical acclaim.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-7)

He made some notable appearances as 'Mkwajo' in award-winning musical _Mo Faya_ directed by [Eric Wainaina](link_14); scheming spouse in _[Facebook](link_15)_ and corrupt politician 'Mzito' in _Ni Sisi_. After several villainous roles, he received the role as stepfather in [MTV](link_16) series [_Shuga 2_](link_17), then as an inspiring soccer coach in _The Inside Story_ aired in Discovery Channel; and a preacher in _The Knife Grinder's Tale_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-8)

In 2016, he was selected for the role as Kenyan crime lord '[Silas Kabaka](link_5)' in the [Netflix](link_18) series _[Sense8](link_5)_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2) The role made him a popular television actor in [Kenya](link_3).

# Trivia

## The Constant Gardener

Edit

When Tessa walks through the slum, numerous children ask her "How are you?" and she responds "I'm fine, how are you?" That scene was unscripted. The children are actual children who live in Kibera, not extras.

Helpful•283 3

Given the subject matter, the Kenyan Government of Kenya proved to be remarkably accommodating to the filmmakers. The Hon. Raphael Tuju, Minister of Information & Communications, stated: "The Constant Gardener is very critical of Kenya, and it was unprecedented that this ministry would support it and license it. But I went ahead and made sure that we did so, because if we didn't support it being filmed here it was still going to be filmed somewhere else, and it would still be critical of Kenya in the past, with respect to issues like corruption."

Helpful•121 0

[Fernando Meirelles](link_50) lobbied to have the movie shot in Kenya, where the story is set, instead of in South Africa, where most of Africa's film industry is located.

Helpful•168 1

Actor [Danny Huston](link_51), cast in the film as the British High Commission's Head of Chancery, Sandy Woodrow, commented: "Modern diplomacy is all about business, and about trying to encourage commercial ventures. I also had a meeting in London with two gentlemen who shall remain nameless, since they worked for [British Secret Service agencies] MI5 and MI6. The more time I spent with them, the more I felt that they  
actually were like the people portrayed in the book. They have an extraordinary, sometimes spectacular way of not answering a question you ask them."

Helpful•98 0

[Ralph Fiennes](link_52) held and operated the camera for Justin Qualye's point-of-view shots. Fiennes is billed in the closing credits for "Justin Quayle POV Camera". As of August 2016, it's Fiennes' only credit in a camera department for a feature film.

_**Transit**_ is a 2005 television [film](link_9) made by [MTV Europe](link_10) and [Tigerlily Films](link_11). It was the first TV movie made by [MTV](link_8).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transit_(2005_film)#cite_note-1)

It was filmed in [St. Petersburg](link_12), [Mexico City](link_13), [Nairobi](link_14) and [Los Angeles](link_15) and shows the lives of 4 people travelling across the globe. During their journeys they think and reason about issues of life such as emotionality and sexuality.

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transit_(2005_film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Transit is presented in a [non-linear narrative](link_16) and follows four main characters from around the world who meet in fortuitous circumstances. The film opens in [Los Angeles](link_15) sometime in 2004, where Asha, an Americanized Indian woman, returns from her trip to [Nairobi](link_14), [Kenya](link_17) and is riding a taxi driving through the freeway.

Six months earlier in [St. Petersburg](link_12), [Russia](link_18). Tatjana, a secretary, is in an abusive relationship with Yuri, a cab driver and drug user. On impulse, she ends the relationship and proceeds to have sex with a Mexican businessman named Ruben, whom she has flirted with in her boss's office to the chagrin of her close friend, Masha.

Tatjana naively believes that Ruben is the man she wants to be with, and so she ends up flying to [Mexico City](link_13) to follow him. Upon tracking his residence, Tatjana is dismayed when a woman holding a baby in her arms states that she is Ruben's wife after saying that she is looking for Ruben. Tatjana goes to a public park to make a call on a payphone and scream her frustrations to Ruben on the phone. Emotionally tired and exhausted from the flight and carrying her large stroller bag around the city in the heat, Tatjana loses consciousness and faints on the spot.

Nearby, a man has observed Tatjana whilst enjoying a picnic with his friends. A brief flashback of two months prior reveals the man to be Jose Luis, nicknamed Champignon ([mushroom](link_19)) or Champy for short, by his handsome yet womanizing friend, Blanco. Champy feels envy and resentment towards Blanco as he is unsuccessful in finding a girlfriend, whilst Blanco already has a relationship but finds time to enjoy infidelities with beautiful women, despite Blanco's good intentions to pair him with women during his secret trips with his mistresses in [Acapulco](link_20).

Champy, however, has landed a job with a brewery company, and the story returns to present time to the picnic with Champy, Blanco, and the rest of their friends to celebrate Champy's new job. When Champy sees Tatjana faint after her phone call, he immediately runs to her side with his friends chasing after him. The group crowds around the unknown girl, and one of Champy's female friends suggest that he take her to his apartment to recover.

In [Los Angeles](link_15), Asha is shown with Vip, her fiancé who is also an Americanized Indian, having lunch to celebrate an event. Asha is a film student on her way to Kenya to shoot her graduation documentary film. Her parents are conservative and traditional [Indian](link_21) people, and they record a heartfelt video message to Asha's uncle and aunt, whom she will be residing with once she arrives in [Nairobi](link_14).

On the eve before her flight, Asha stumbles upon a sex tape of Vip with one of his female Caucasian colleagues she found while preparing to follow Vip to a nightclub where he his partying with his friends. Hurt by this betrayal, she goes to the nightclub and witnesses with her very eyes that Vip is indeed not the man she knows. The couple argue outside the club and Asha terminates their engagement after it is further revealed that Vip has had more than one instance of his sexual liaisons with other women.

During their fight, Champy is seen by his car packing things in the trunk. The scene then cuts to Champy and Asha in an empty [bar](link_22), with Champy writing down his contact details on his company's promotional sticky note paper and give it to Asha.

In [Nairobi](link_14), Asha is living with her relatives. Her documentary project comes to a temporary obstacle, with her original concept scrapped because of lack of funds from her documentary subject, and she is frustrated at having to start over and look for a new story angle. The story also introduces Matthew, a local who is into the burgeoning hip-hop culture of Nairobi.

## About the film

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transit_(2005_film)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: About the film")]

[MTV Europe](link_10) and [Tigerlily Films](link_11) produced this film to air directly on television on all [MTV Networks](link_23) on 1 December, the [World AIDS Day](link_24).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transit_(2005_film)#cite_note-2) Its goal is to make teenagers think about matters such as [sex](link_25) and [relationships](link_26).

_Transit_ was made as part of MTV's [Staying Alive](link_27) campaign, which aims to raise [HIV](link_28) awareness and reduce [discrimination](link_29) against [HIV positive individuals](link_30).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transit_(2005_film)#cite_note-3) The movie was partially funded by the [Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency](link_31).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transit_(2005_film)#cite_note-4)

The film is also available as a free download via the Staying Alive website. Unfortunately this was removed when MTV and the Staying Alive Foundation changed the design of their website in 2008, for the 27th World AIDS Day since the virus, HIV, that eventually leads to the development of AIDS, was discovered. The film Transit can now be found to watch on YouTube.

**Anthony Dwane Mackie** (born September 23, 1978) is an American actor. He has appeared in [blockbuster films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockbuster_(entertainment) "Blockbuster (entertainment)") and [independent features](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_film "Independent film"), and has [received accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Anthony_Mackie "List of awards and nominations received by Anthony Mackie") such as nominations for two [Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Awards "Emmy Awards") and a [Screen Actors Guild Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actor_Awards "Actor Awards").

Mackie was born in [New Orleans, Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans,_Louisiana "New Orleans, Louisiana") and studied acting at [Juilliard School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juilliard_School "Juilliard School"), receiving a [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") in drama in 2001. He began his career appearing in a handful of stage productions, and made his film debut in [_8 Mile_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8_Mile_(film) "8 Mile (film)") (2002). While developing his career in films such as _[Million Dollar Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Million\_Dollar\_Baby "Million Dollar Baby")_ (2004), [_Half Nelson_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_Nelson_(film) "Half Nelson (film)") (2006), [_Notorious_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notorious_(2009_film) "Notorious (2009 film)") (2009), and _[Real Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real\_Steel "Real Steel")_ (2011), he garnered critical acclaim and several awards for headlining _[Brother to Brother](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brother\_to\_Brother\_(film) "Brother to Brother (film)")_ (2004) and co-starring in _[The Hurt Locker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hurt\_Locker "The Hurt Locker")_ (2008).

Mackie achieved global stardom portraying [Sam Wilson / Falcon / Captain America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Wilson_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Sam Wilson (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") in the [Marvel Cinematic Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe") (MCU), beginning with _

**Humberto Busto Marín** (born 23 June 1978) is a Mexican actor.

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Humberto_Busto&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Busto got his first major role in 1999, playing Jorge in the film _[Amores perros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amores\_perros "Amores perros")_, released in 2000.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-1)

Busto's performance as Heriberto in _Oso Polar_ won him awards for Best Actor in the 15th [Morelia International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morelia_International_Film_Festival "Morelia International Film Festival")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-2) and the 5th Quito Latin American Film Festival,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-3) as well as an [Ariel Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariel_Award "Ariel Award") nomination.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-4)

He has been recognized as well for his work behind the camera. Under his direction, _La teta de Botero_ (2014) and _Julkita_ (2017) were winners of Best Short Narrative Made in Mexico award of the [Oaxaca FilmFest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oaxaca_FilmFest "Oaxaca FilmFest").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-6)

From 2010 to 2012, Busto portrayed the fastidious and self-important Apolinar Caborca in the three seasons of the television series _[Los héroes del norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_h%C3%A9roes\_del\_norte "Los héroes del norte")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-7)

Humberto Busto has a degree in Dramatic Arts from the University Theater Center of the [National Autonomous University of Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Autonomous_University_of_Mexico "National Autonomous University of Mexico"). He is an alumnus of [Berlinale Talents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlinale_Talents "Berlinale Talents")[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-8) and studied for a master's degree in film production at [California State University, Northridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_University,_Northridge "California State University, Northridge").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-auto-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-10)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Humberto_Busto&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Personal life")]

In a 2012 interview, he indirectly affirmed that he was [bisexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisexuality "Bisexuality") when asked if he had felt attraction to both men and women, to which he replied, "Yes, of course! I fall in love with squirrels."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-11) Seven years later, in July 2019, he was seen actively participating in the march for sexual diversity held in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-12) Five years later, in July 2024, he came out as [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay "Gay"), also sharing that he suffered from [bullying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullying "Bullying") in his childhood because of his sexual orientation.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-14)

[lovemoreself](https://www.imdb.com/user/p.xeazg45eydnshlr5mr7o5qblsq/?ref_=tturv_c_1_uname)10*   Aug 31, 2005

#### [Meirelles, Weisz and Fiennes make a modern political masterpiece.](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0387131/reviews/?featured=rw1162410&ref_=tturv_c_1_hd)

Intelligent and moving political thriller that should be held right up there with "All The Presidents Men" and "The Killing Fields " as one of the best political thrillers ever made. Fernando Meirelles tops his last directional effort with a thriller that is moving, scary and down right forthright in it's views of big companies gone wrong and the horrors that they are willing to inflect on others for the sake of profit. Rachel Weisz and Ralph Fiennes give career best performances in this film and that's a huge compliment considering the fact that they are good in almost everything they do, even in bad movies. Weisz is strong willed and obsessive and Fiennes is determine and endearing and both of them compliment each other with there destine to be award winning chemistry and acting chops. The director compliments both of them with a view of Africa that is rarely seen in film and a sense of reality that is only found in real life.  
  
Rachel Weisz, Ralph Fiennes and Fernando Meirelles all should be honored at award season for their amazing efforts in this film because as of right now, this is with out a doubt the film to beat come Oscar time.

[rayoduck](https://www.imdb.com/user/p.wxufyr53kc57riy22tyylygmkq/?ref_=tturv_c_2_uname)10*   Sep 1, 2005

#### [Haunting, Heartfelt and Horrifying](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0387131/reviews/?featured=rw1162979&ref_=tturv_c_2_hd)

Slow tension building thriller that is charge even more with the great performances of Rachel Weisz and Ralph Fiennes, who both bring an essence of realism to their roles and a sense of chemistry that is really not found in movies like this anymore. Rachel Weisz brings a ferry fury that is ripe in it's convictions and Ralph Fiennes brings a cool, collective zeal that is a slow building timer ready to emotionally exploded at any minute. Both performances compliment the fine directing of Fernando Meirelles, who gives this tale a sense of brilliance in its storytelling and a sense of the way the world really works. It's a heartfelt story of lost and redemption and it's hauntingly poetic in it's horrifying look at the horrors of a world that is willing to cast a blind eye at the problems of big business and corrupt governments that are willing to do anything in order to make a fast buck. Even going as far than to destroy human life to achieve their goals.  
  
This is a brilliant film and I can't wait to see it again.

[![Image 4: Avatar](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjQzNTQyNzQ4M15BMl5BanBnXkFtZTgwNTMyMzE0MDE@._V1_QL75_UX24_CR0,0,24,24_.jpg) Tony-Kiss-Castillo](https://www.imdb.com/user/p.3cm6u7vocv573q3yewb3ik3ia4/?ref_=tturv_c_3_uname)9*   Dec 19, 2023

#### [CONSTANCY INEVITABLY UNEARTHS THE TRUTH!](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0387131/reviews/?featured=rw9504417&ref_=tturv_c_3_hd)

The Constant Gardener shines with great intensity, but in a way that is rather subtle, somewhat occult, just beneath the surface.  
  
It's the kind of "Thriller" where more often than not, a silent expression or a nervous pause communicates more than a hundred words of dialogue! Directed with panache, intrigue and passion in both scope and focus by Brazilian Fernando Meirelles (City of God), has created a tale of international dimensions!  
  
Based on the work of John le Carré, Gardener shows us the sinister side of pharmaceutical multinationals, where human life in Third World countries serves to supply their perverse drug trials, in pursuit of ever bigger record profits!  
  
Rachel Weisz (The Mummy, The Mummy Returns, Constantine) has been awarded a much-deserved Golden Globe for Best Supporting Actress for her role as activist and wife. Also, Ms. Weisz most certainly deserved her Oscar win! The subtlety, complexity, originality and freshness of her portrayal are nothing short of amazing.  
  
Ralph Fiennes (The English Patient, Maid in Manhattan), despite giving one of the best performances of his life, curiously, did not even receive a Golden Globe nomination!!!  
  
GARDNER demonstrates clearly to us that often the reality of things is not what it seems at first glance.  
  
Justin Quayle (Fiennes) is a mid-level diplomat. He is tormented by persistent rumors and some strong indications of frequent infidelities by his activist wife. When she becomes the victim of a violent and gruesome murder, perhaps at the hands of her alleged African lover, Qualye senses something is askance and begins a methodical and patient investigation. To the extent that he gradually inches closer to the truth, threats and pressures to desist his inquiry increase exponentially!  
  
But as secrets of his late wife's life continue to be revealed, her image has changed completely; Mr. Quayle has become obsessed with arriving at the truth, regardless of the consequences. Also, Quayle, now quite repentant for having doubted his wife to the extent he did, now comes to realize that the most suitable place for him would have been beside the wife who loved him so dearly!.  
  
Thusly, Gardener combines several diverse elements like suspense, political intrigue, romance, action, research and international outreach with masterful skill and powerful intensity.  
  
9*********...ENJOY!.../...DISFRUTELA!!  
  
Any comments, questions or suggestions, in English o en Español are most welcome!

[yolanda_flcn](https://www.imdb.com/user/p.6ynt3kmhaqpg2o7k6aceldsquy/?ref_=tturv_c_4_uname)7*   Sep 2, 2005

#### [Great Great film.](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0387131/reviews/?featured=rw1163725&ref_=tturv_c_4_hd)

I thought the movie was great and worthy of the praise it has been getting from audiences and critics alike. Ralph Fiennes gives the performance of his career as a grieving man looking for answers and is slowing discovering the corruption all around him and Rachel Weisz steals the film whole heartily with a really deserving Oscar worthy performance as a human rights activist who will stop at nothing to get at the truth. The story is pretty scary and the cinematography is fantastic. Yes, the shaky camera can get in the way but it's not distracting enough to ruin the film.  
  
If you want to see a movie that will make you think, this is it.

Best known for her iconic portrayal as Melisandre in the global phenomenon, Game of Thrones, Emmy Award-nominated Carice van Houten is one of Europe's most celebrated actors.  
  
Dutch born Carice first earned widespread critical acclaim for her award-winning performance in Paul Verhoeven's Black Book in 2006. Other notable international credits include Bryan Singer's Valkyrie in which she starred opposite Tom Cruise, Bill Condon's The Fifth Estate, and Martin Koolhoven's Brimstone alongside Guy Pearce.  
  
In her native Netherlands, the role of Lea in Antoinette Beumer's The Happy Housewife earned Carice a record-breaking fifth Golden Calf award. She also received a best actress award at the Tribeca Festival for her portrayal of Ingrid Jonker in Paula van der Oest's Black Butterflies. Further credits include Joram Lürsen's Love is All which broke Dutch box office records, and the titular role in the much loved Dutch children's film Minoes.  
  
Between 2019 and 2021 Carice starred in the Dutch television series, Red Light, which she co-created with Halina Reijn. The show uses a narrative lense to explore human trafficking, prostitution, and organized crime. Carice also starred in and co-produced the Dutch indie film, Instinct, which won the Variety Piazza Grande Award at the Locarno Film Festival. She also starred in in the international TV series Temple alongside Mark Strong, as well as the television adaptation of Dangerous Liaisons.  
  
Carice will next be seen opposite David Duchovny and Jack Whitehall in the television series, Malice, a psychological thriller about a seemingly happy family whose darkest secrets are revealed and exploited when they unwittingly open their home to a charismatic stranger.  
  
2026 will also see her star in Mees Peijnenburg's A Family which is co-produced by Lukas Dhont's The Reunion.

Actor Ralph Nathaniel Twisleton-Wykeham-Fiennes was born on December 22, 1962 in Suffolk, England, to Jennifer Anne Mary Alleyne (Lash), a novelist, and Mark Fiennes, a photographer. He is the eldest of six children. Four of his siblings are also in the arts: [Martha Fiennes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0276397/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), a director; [Magnus Fiennes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0276396/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), a musician; [Sophie Fiennes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0276400/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), a producer; and [Joseph Fiennes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001212/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), an actor. He is of English, Irish, and Scottish origin.  
  
A noted Shakespeare interpreter, he first achieved success onstage at the Royal National Theatre. Fiennes first worked on screen in 1990 and then made his film debut in 1992 as Heathcliff in Emily Brontë's [Wuthering Heights (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0104181/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), opposite Juliette Binoche. 1993 was his "breakout year". He had a major role in the controversial Peter Greenaway film [The Baby of Mâcon (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0106335/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), with Julia Ormond, which was poorly received. Later that year he became known internationally for portraying the amoral Nazi concentration camp commandant Amon Goeth in Steven Spielberg's [Schindler's List (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108052/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). For this he was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor and the Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor. He did not win, but did win the Best Supporting Actor BAFTA Award for the role, as well as Best Supporting Actor honors from numerous critics groups, including the National Society of Film Critics, and the New York, Chicago, Boston, and London Film Critics associations. His portrayal as Göth also earned him a spot on the American Film Institute's list of Top 50 Film Villains. To look suitable to represent Goeth, Fiennes gained weight, but he managed to shed it afterwards. In 1994, he portrayed American academic Charles Van Doren in [Quiz Show (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0110932/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). In 1996, he was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actor for his performance as Count Almásy the World War II epic romance, and another Best Picture winner, [Anthony Minghella](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005237/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s [The English Patient (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0116209/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), in which he starred with Kristin Scott Thomas. He also received BAFTA and Golden Globe nominations, as well as two Screen Actors Guild (SAG) Award nominations, one for Best Actor and another shared with the film's ensemble cast.  
  
Since then, Fiennes has been in a number of notable films, including [Strange Days (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0114558/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Oscar and Lucinda (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119843/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), the animated [The Prince of Egypt (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120794/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [István Szabó](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0843640/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s [Sunshine (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0145503/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Neil Jordan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001403/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)-directed films [The End of the Affair (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0172396/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [The Good Thief (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0780536/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [The Reader (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0976051/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), co-starring [Kate Winslet](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000701/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Kathryn Bigelow](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000941/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s Oscar®-winning [The Hurt Locker (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2278388/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).  
  
He is also known for his roles in major film franchises such as the Harry Potter film series (2005-2011), in which he played the evil Lord Voldemort. His nephew, [Hero Fiennes Tiffin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2842005/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) played Tom Riddle, the young Lord Voldemort, in [Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0417741/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). **Peter King Nzioki Mwania** (born 25 May 1978), popularly known as **Peter King**, is a Kenyan actor.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2) He is best known for his roles in the films _[The Constant Gardener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Constant\_Gardener\_(film) "The Constant Gardener (film)")_, _[The Fifth Estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fifth\_Estate\_(film) "The Fifth Estate (film)")_ and _[Sense8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense8 "Sense8")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Nzioki&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Nzioki was born on 25 May 1978 in [Nairobi, Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"). His father Michael David Mwania, served in the [Kenyan Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Army "Kenya Army") and his mother worked at the military hospital. At the age of six, he joined church productions at the [Lang’ata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lang'ata "Lang'ata") Barracks. He completed his education from Lang’ata High School in [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-kenyabuzz-3)

He is married to fellow actress Tess King.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-4)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Nzioki&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

He made his acting debut in 2000 at the [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") National Theatre for three years under the guidance of Joab Kanuka. In theater, he played 'Iago' in the Phoenix Players production of the [Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare") tragedy _[Othello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Othello "Othello")_. In 2005, he made his film debut with a minor role in _[The Constant Gardener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Constant\_Gardener\_(film) "The Constant Gardener (film)")_ directed by [Fernando Meirelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Meirelles "Fernando Meirelles").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-kenyabuzz-3) In the same year, he appeared as 'Barman' in the television movie _[Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transit\_(2005\_film) "Transit (2005 film)")_. In 2016, he appeared in the thriller film _[The CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_CEO "The CEO")_ where he played the role of 'Jomo'. The film had its premier 10 July 2016, at the Eko Hotels & Suites, [Victoria Island, Lagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Island,_Lagos "Victoria Island, Lagos")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-5) and later received critical acclaim.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-7)

He made some notable appearances as 'Mkwajo' in award-winning musical _Mo Faya_ directed by [Eric Wainaina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Wainaina_(musician) "Eric Wainaina (musician)"); scheming spouse in _[Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook")_ and corrupt politician 'Mzito' in _Ni Sisi_. After several villainous roles, he received the role as stepfather in [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV") series [_Shuga 2_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shuga_(TV_series) "Shuga (TV series)"), then as an inspiring soccer coach in _The Inside Story_ aired in Discovery Channel; and a preacher in _The Knife Grinder's Tale_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-8)

In 2016, he was selected for the role as Kenyan crime lord '[Silas Kabaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense8 "Sense8")' in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") series _[Sense8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense8 "Sense8")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2) The role made him a popular television actor in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya").

**Humberto Busto Marín** (born 23 June 1978) is a Mexican actor.

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Humberto_Busto&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Busto got his first major role in 1999, playing Jorge in the film _[Amores perros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amores\_perros "Amores perros")_, released in 2000.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-1)

Busto's performance as Heriberto in _Oso Polar_ won him awards for Best Actor in the 15th [Morelia International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morelia_International_Film_Festival "Morelia International Film Festival")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-2) and the 5th Quito Latin American Film Festival,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-3) as well as an [Ariel Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariel_Award "Ariel Award") nomination.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-4)

He has been recognized as well for his work behind the camera. Under his direction, _La teta de Botero_ (2014) and _Julkita_ (2017) were winners of Best Short Narrative Made in Mexico award of the [Oaxaca FilmFest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oaxaca_FilmFest "Oaxaca FilmFest").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-6)

From 2010 to 2012, Busto portrayed the fastidious and self-important Apolinar Caborca in the three seasons of the television series _[Los héroes del norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_h%C3%A9roes\_del\_norte "Los héroes del norte")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-7)

Humberto Busto has a degree in Dramatic Arts from the University Theater Center of the [National Autonomous University of Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Autonomous_University_of_Mexico "National Autonomous University of Mexico"). He is an alumnus of [Berlinale Talents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlinale_Talents "Berlinale Talents")[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-8) and studied for a master's degree in film production at [California State University, Northridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_University,_Northridge "California State University, Northridge").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-auto-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-10)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Humberto_Busto&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Personal life")]

In a 2012 interview, he indirectly affirmed that he was [bisexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisexuality "Bisexuality") when asked if he had felt attraction to both men and women, to which he replied, "Yes, of course! I fall in love with squirrels."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-11) Seven years later, in July 2019, he was seen actively participating in the march for sexual diversity held in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-12) Five years later, in July 2024, he came out as [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay "Gay"), also sharing that he suffered from [bullying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullying "Bullying") in his childhood because of his sexual orientation.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Busto#cite_note-14)
