The [Old Summer Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Summer_Palace "Old Summer Palace") was looted and burnt by a combined Anglo-French expeditionary force during the [Second Opium War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Opium_War "Second Opium War"). Among the artifacts stolen are [twelve bronze heads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiyantang "Haiyantang") of the animals of the [Chinese zodiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac "Chinese zodiac").

In the present day, the bronze heads, supplied by MP Corporation are all auctioned. JC is tasked by MP to find the remaining lost bronze heads, with a promise of a 10 million dollar bonus, if he can recover all of them, including the Dragon. He visits Professor Guan, who had created 12 identical replicas for study purposes with his team of researchers, under the guise of a reporter named Martin from [National Geographic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Geographic_Society "National Geographic Society").

JC scans the animal heads using special gloves so that his secret organisation can replicate an extremely realistic model of them. After scanning, he goes to Paris to find a woman named Coco, recommended by Guan, for more information on the whereabouts of two bronze heads. JC and his partners infiltrate a mansion to find two of the bronze heads. JC manages to decode the password to a top secret vault and finds the bronze heads, a painting called "The Roses", along with many other valuable national treasures thought to be lost inside and manages to evade capture with all the valuables despite being busted. However, he is spotted by Coco. Having no time to explain himself, he tells Coco to meet him at a boat house while fleeing from the mansion's security.

At the boat house, Martin tells Coco that he is working for a secret corporation that is trying to recover all the lost relics for China. The guards from the mansion storm the boat house and try to attack JC, but the police are called in and they are all arrested. JC, Coco and Simon are cleared of any wrongdoing and are released. JC and his team are invited to a castle owned by a lady named Catherine, unaware that the guards from the mansion are tailing them out of suspicion. It turns out that the captain of the "Indestructible", one of the ships involved in the destruction of the Old Summer Palace, is Catherine's great-great-grandfather. This upsets Coco, who confronts Catherine on it. JC and his team find many treasures in the castle, including the bronze head of the [Rooster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rooster_(zodiac) "Rooster (zodiac)"), and hatch a series of plans to ferry them out.

JC promises Catherine that he will help her locate her great-great-grandfather's remains. The next day, they venture out in search of the Indestructible's treasures, located on a seemingly uninhabited island. JC instructs Coco and Catherine to stay behind while his team explore the island. Coco and Catherine however disobey JC's orders to look for the remains on their own. They get entangled among the vines, forcing JC to rescue them. While exhuming the great-great grandfather's remains, the group accidentally discovers the remains of the Indestructible, several more bronze heads and a large quantity of gold. As they prepare to leave with all the artifacts, the guards from the mansion confront them. In turn, the island's local inhabitants, a group of pirates, appear and promptly capture everyone.

JC and his team fight their way through, escaping the island via a log set up with a pulley system, leaving the five guards with the pirates. On the yacht, Coco accidentally discovers the real motive of JC's ventures and confronts him. The log carrying approximately eight tonnes of gold sinks. Nevertheless, JC and his team still get rewarded for recovering some of the lost bronze heads. The group are enraged when they find out that the supposedly-missing [Dragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon_(zodiac) "Dragon (zodiac)") head was already at the hands of MP Corp all along, thereby making it impossible to claim the large bonus. Coco and her fellow students' protests over the sale of the national treasures escalate quickly and capture worldwide attention. As Coco's students try to find out more about MP Corp, three of them, including Coco's younger brother, are captured.

After Coco asks JC for help, JC contacts MP Corp on the availability of "The Roses" painting and is allowed into the secret premises. Having toured the entire factory where almost exact duplicates of the relics are made to be sold as real relics in auctions, JC deduces the location of the captives. He challenges a long time rival who happens to be there as well — unscrupulous treasure hunter, Vulture, to a fight but it ends in a stalemate. JC bargains with MP Corp to sell "The Roses" at a discounted price and secure the release of the three hostages. When MP Corp refuses, JC fights his way to the chamber. A furnace explodes due to a guard's baton rupturing one of the pipes, destroying most of the facility. JC then settles for the release of the three hostages in exchange for the painting and not paying damages done to the premises.

Meanwhile, the [Dragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon_(zodiac) "Dragon (zodiac)") bronze head is expected to fetch the highest price; however, no one bids for it due to increasing pressure from activist groups. MP Corp, to teach these groups a lesson, threatens to throw the relic into an active volcano, calling the mission "Let the Dragon Fly", if no bids are received by noon the next day. The deadline passes without a single bid and Vulture leads a group of three sky divers to throw the relic into the volcano. JC intervenes in order to save the relic from dropping into the volcano, and is severely injured in the ensuing airborne struggle. As a mark of respect, Vulture hands over the relic to a sprawled JC. MP Corp's owners are arrested on possession of "The Roses" painting. JC is seen recovering in a hospital and on good terms with everyone, including Vulture, and also reunites with his wife, who visits him in the hospital.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=CZ12&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Jackie_Chan_2012_Jelgava.jpg/250px-Jackie_Chan_2012_Jelgava.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jackie_Chan_2012_Jelgava.jpg)

Jackie Chan on the set at [Jelgava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jelgava "Jelgava"), [Latvia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvia "Latvia").

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") began on 5 June 2011.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-filming-14) From 18 April to 2 May 2012, Jackie Chan filmed several scenes in the [Aerodium Latvia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerodium_Latvia "Aerodium Latvia")[vertical wind tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertical_wind_tunnel "Vertical wind tunnel") in [Jelgava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jelgava "Jelgava"), [Latvia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvia "Latvia").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-15) Filming also took place in [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France"), [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"), [Taiwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan "Taiwan") and [Vanuatu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanuatu "Vanuatu"). Chan did most of the stunts and fight scenes himself with little support from his stunt team. [Jean-Yves Blondeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Yves_Blondeau "Jean-Yves Blondeau"), the inventor of the skate suit, trained Chan to use the suit for the film's body blading sequence.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-16) This film was simultaneously made in [IMAX 3D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX_3D "IMAX 3D").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-17) Filming officially wrapped up on 8 May the same year.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-filming-14)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-18)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=CZ12&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Release")]

The gala premier of the film was held on 12 December 2012;[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-19) it was released across Asia on 20 December and in India on 28 December.

### U.S. release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=CZ12&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: U.S. release")]

_CZ12_ was originally scheduled for release in U.S. theaters sometime in the summer of 2013 with about 20 minutes edited out by Jackie Chan himself in order to optimize the pace and content for North American audiences.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-20) This release date was pushed back to the fall; the re-edited version was released on 18 October for theatrical exhibit exclusively by [AMC Theatres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_Theatres "AMC Theatres").

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=CZ12&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Reception")]

In competition with films from abroad _CZ12_ grossed HK$11.7 million (US$1.5 million),[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-21) as well as becoming the top-ranked Chinese film at the Taiwan box office.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-22) The film debuted second in mainland China (after _[Lost in Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost\_in\_Thailand "Lost in Thailand")_), going on to gross over US$145 million at the box office and emerging to be one of the highest grossing domestic films in China.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-24)

### Criticism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=CZ12&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Criticism")]

_[Time Out Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_Out\_(magazine) "Time Out (magazine)")_ gave the film two stars out of five referring to the film as "a pedestrian film by any measure aside from its action design".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-26) The _[South China Morning Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South\_China\_Morning\_Post "South China Morning Post")_ gave the film one and a half stars out of five, noting that "_CZ12_ lumbers like a cheap DVD knock-off of one of [Jackie Chan's] old classics" and "_CZ12_ is like watching a former star athlete struggle in a meaningless game".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-27)

_[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ also gave a negative review, noting the film's length and the lack of martial arts and stunts that star Chan is known for.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-hr-review-8)_[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ gave the film a negative review as well, stating "Jackie Chan emerges a Jackie-of-all-trades and master of none in [_CZ12_]".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CZ12#cite_note-variety-7)

# Chinese Zodiac Years Chart

 Each Chinese lunar year has a Chinese zodiac sign, hence also called Chinese zodiac year. As the [lunar calendar](https://www.travelchinaguide.com/intro/focus/calendar.htm) does not agree perfectly with the Gregorian calendar, the Chinese zodiac year is a little different from the Gregorian year. The below Chinese zodiac chart helps you find out what is your Chinese zodiac year and the accurate starting and ending dates of the Chinese zodiac years.  
  
2025 is the Chinese zodiac Snake year. In Gregorian calendar, it is from Jan. 29, 2025 to Feb. 16, 2026.

# Chinese Zodiac

Chinese zodiac, or shengxiao (/shnng-sshyao/ 'born resembling'), is represented by **12 zodiac animals**. In order, they are the Rat, Ox, Tiger, Rabbit, Dragon, Snake, Horse, Goat, Monkey, Rooster, Dog, and Pig.

Chinese zodiac years begin/end at Chinese New Year (in January/February). Each year in the repeating zodiac cycle of 12 years is represented by a zodiac animal, each with its own reputed attributes.

**2026** is the [year of the Horse](https://www.chinahighlights.com/travelguide/chinese-zodiac/horse.htm), starting from February 17th, 2026 to February 5th, 2027.

**2027** is the [Year of the Goat](https://www.chinahighlights.com/travelguide/chinese-zodiac/goat.htm), starting from February 6th, 2027, to January 25th, 2028.

Chinese people believe that a person's horoscope, personality, and love compatibility are closely associated with his/her Chinese zodiac sign, determined by his/her birth year.

Here you can learn all about the Chinese zodiac, including your Chinese zodiac sign, your horoscope predictions for 2026 and 2027.

## Chinese Zodiac Signs' Personality

Chinese zodiac animals have astrological and cultural meanings. Chinese people associate each animal sign with certain characteristics. It's believed that people born in a given year have the personality of that year's animal.

*   **Rat**: quick-witted, resourceful, versatile, kind.
*   **Ox**: diligent, dependable, strong, determined.
*   **Tiger**: brave, confident, competitive, unpredictable.
*   **Rabbit**: quiet, elegant, kind, responsible.
*   **Dragon**: confident, intelligent, enthusiastic.
*   **Snake**: enigmatic, intelligent, wise.
*   **Horse**: animated, active, energetic.
*   **Goat**: calm, gentle, sympathetic.
*   **Monkey**: sharp, smart, curious.
*   **Rooster**: observant, hardworking, courageous.
*   **Dog**: lovely, honest, prudent.
*   **Pig**: compassionate, generous, diligent.

## What is the luckiest/unluckiest Chinese zodiac sign?

In Chinese culture, the top 5 luckiest/most popular zodiac signs are [**Dragon**](https://www.chinahighlights.com/travelguide/chinese-zodiac/dragon.htm), [**Snake**](https://www.chinahighlights.com/travelguide/chinese-zodiac/snake.htm), [**Pig**](https://www.chinahighlights.com/travelguide/chinese-zodiac/pig.htm), [**Rat**](https://www.chinahighlights.com/travelguide/chinese-zodiac/rat.htm), and [**Tiger**](https://www.chinahighlights.com/travelguide/chinese-zodiac/tiger.htm) conventionally.

There is a popular Chinese folk saying that 9/10 Goats are inadequate (十羊九不全 '10 Goats 9 incomplete'), which implies that most people born in a year of the Goat are destined for bad luck. Most Chinese people also believe that people born in a Goat year will grow up to be followers rather than leaders. Although this is an outdated superstition, it has a real effect on Chinese society.

## Chinese Zodiac Story: Explaining the Order and Why There's No Cat

![Image 42: Star Zodiac Signs and Chinese Zodiac Signs](https://data.chinahighlights.com/grey.gif)

Do you know why the 12 Chinese zodiac animals are in their fixed sequence from Rat to Pig?

The sequence of the 12 signs is popularly explained by a myth about when the Jade Emperor (the supreme immortal) wanted to select 12 animals to be his guards. All creatures on Earth were summoned to participate in a race. The earlier one went through the Heavenly Gate, the better the rank one would have.

*   **Rat**and **Ox** got up very early. On the way to the Gate, Rat jumped onto the back of the Ox to cross the river. He won first place by suddenly jumping down from Ox's back and dashed to the feet of the Emperor when they're near to the Heavenly Gate. Ox was second.
*   **Tiger** and **Rabbit** came third and fourth because both are fast and competitive, but Tiger was faster.
*   Good-looking **Dragon** was fifth and was immediately noticed by the Jade Emperor, who said Dragon's son could be sixth. Just then, **Snake** came forward and said Dragon was his adoptive father; so Snake ranked sixth.
*   **Horse** and **Goat** arrived. They were very kind and modest and each let the other go first. They were ranked seventh and eighth.
*   **Monkey** had fallen well behind. But he jumped between trees and stones, and caught up to be ninth. Last were **Rooster**, **Dog**, and **Pig**.

**Why is the cat not one of the 12 Chinese zodiac animals**? It is said that Cat and Rat got as far as crossing the river together on Ox's back, but Rat pushed Cat into the water. Cat was washed away and didn't get to the Heavenly Gate in time to get a ranking. After that a great enmity grew between Cat and Rat, so that rats scatter in all directions when a cat appears.

The story is widespread (and widely varying) among Chinese. Though it is made up, it might be interesting for you to tell your children and friends.

Actually, the 12 Chinese zodiac animals were chosen very deliberately by the ancients, after many revisions. The zodiac animals are either closely related to ancient Chinese people's daily lives or have lucky meanings in ancient Chinese culture.

## What are the differences between Chinese zodiac and western astrology?

![Image 43: Star Zodiac Signs and Chinese Zodiac Signs](https://data.chinahighlights.com/grey.gif)

The main similarity between the two systems is that both systems are based on time periods of birth, and they both have 12 symbols or signs with associated personalities and fortunes.

However, there are big differences in their origins and astrological theory.

With the **Chinese zodiac**, the 12 signs are derived from the ancients' musings about archetypal animals, people's personalities and fortunes, and their relationships with one another and years of birth. A myth about a celestial race was later developed to explain the Chinese zodiac sequence.

This differs from **Western astrology**, where the 12 zodiac signs are based on constellations' positions relative to the earth. The constellations were named according to Greek mythology and astrological theory was developed based on the stars supposed influence on human personalities and lives.

In addition, the Chinese zodiac is calculated on a year-by-year base while the Western zodiac corresponds with "months".

The **Chinese zodiac** is a traditional classification scheme based on the [Chinese calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_calendar "Chinese calendar") that assigns an animal and its reputed attributes to each year in a repeating twelve-year (or duodenary) cycle.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-1) The zodiac is very important in [Chinese culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_culture "Chinese culture") as a reflection of traditional [Chinese philosophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_philosophy "Chinese philosophy").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-2) Chinese folkways held that one's personality is related to the attributes of their zodiac animal.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-3) Originating from [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"), the zodiac and its variations remain popular in many [East Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Asia "East Asia"), [Central Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Asia "Central Asia") and [Southeast Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Asia "Southeast Asia")[countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_state "Sovereign state"), such as [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan"),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-4)[South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-:0-5)[Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam "Vietnam"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-:0-5)[Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-6), [Kazakhstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakhstan "Kazakhstan"), [Kyrgyzstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrgyzstan "Kyrgyzstan"), [Mongolia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongolia "Mongolia"), [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey"), and [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore"), and among immigrants from these countries.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-7)

Identifying this scheme as a "_[zodiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac "Zodiac")_" reflects superficial similarities to the [Western zodiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_astrology "Western astrology"): both divide time cycles into twelve parts, label the majority of those parts with animals, and are used to ascribe a person's personality or events in their life to the person's particular relationship to the cycle. The 12 Chinese zodiac animals in the cycle are not only used to represent years in China but are also believed to influence people's personalities, careers, compatibility, marriages, and fortunes.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-8)

For the starting date of a zodiac year, there are two schools of thought in [Chinese astrology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_astrology "Chinese astrology"): [Chinese New Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_New_Year "Chinese New Year") or the [start of spring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lichun "Lichun").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chinese_zodiac&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

There might be a discussion about this on [the talk page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Chinese_zodiac "Talk:Chinese zodiac")._(February 2024)_ _([Learn how and when to remove this message](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Maintenance\_template\_removal "Help:Maintenance template removal"))_

Some scholars suggest the twelve animals were chosen for their symbolic traits, based on their revered status in traditional Chinese culture. The choice varied regionally before being standardized in the [Han Dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_dynasty "Han dynasty"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-9) when the Chinese zodiac, as an essential part of Chinese culture, started to take shape. This era formalizes a twelve-year cycle, where each year is associated with a specific animal, as part of a timekeeping system. This system, known as the zodiac cycle, combined the twelve _Earthly Branches_ (地支) with the ten _Heavenly Stems_ (天干) to create a 60-year cycle, a cyclical timekeeping system seen as embodying both personality traits and the broader society. Each Earthly Branch was linked to one of the twelve zodiac signs and to an animal: Rat, Ox, Tiger, Rabbit, Dragon, Snake, Horse, Goat, Monkey, Rooster, Dog, and Pig.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-10)

According to legend, the [Jade Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jade_Emperor "Jade Emperor") held a contest to decide which animals would be lucky enough to be included in the calendar. The winner of the race – the rat – received the first year of the 12-year cycle, and so on.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-11)

However, historical research[_[by whom?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Words\_to\_watch#Unsupported\_attributions "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch")_] suggests that the Chinese zodiac emerged after the establishment of the "Ganzhi or Sexagenary cycle",[_[when?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_] with each of the twelve animals directly assigned to one of the twelve Earthly Branches. In this system, a person's birth year determines their associated animal, which is linked to a specific Earthly Branch and serves both a chronological function and a means of categorizing individuals into symbolic groups, akin to a genus.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In the [Eastern Han dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Han_dynasty "Eastern Han dynasty"), [Xu Shen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xu_Shen "Xu Shen") said that the character _si_ (巳) was the image of a snake, and the same was true for _hai_ (亥) and _shi_ (豕; 'pig'). Since the twelve [Earthly Branches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthly_Branches "Earthly Branches") of the zodiac were easily confused, people replaced them with animals and borrowed the ordinal symbols to match them with the Earthly Branches to form a chronological symbol system.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-12)

In "Totem and celestial combination theory", it is suggested that the zodiac is ancient animal totem worship combined with astronomical images in astronomy.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In [Chinese astrology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_astrology "Chinese astrology") the animal signs assigned by **year** represent self-presentation or perception by others.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] It is a common misconception that the animals assigned by year are the only signs, and many [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_culture "Western culture") descriptions of Chinese astrology only reference this system. There are also animal signs assigned by **month** (called "inner animals"), by **day** (called "true animals"), and **hours** (called "secret animals"). The [Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_(Wu_Xing) "Earth (Wu Xing)") is all twelve signs, with five seasons.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[Michel Ferlus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Ferlus "Michel Ferlus") (2013) notes that the Old Chinese names of the earthly branches are of [Austroasiatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austroasiatic_languages "Austroasiatic languages") origin.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-Ferlus2013-16) Some of Ferlus's comparisons are given below, with Old Chinese reconstructions cited from Baxter & Sagart (2014).[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-17)

*   [丑](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E4%B8%91 "wikt:丑"): [Old Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Chinese "Old Chinese") *[n̥]ruʔ (compare Proto-[Viet-Muong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietic_languages "Vietic languages") *c.luː '[water buffalo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_buffalo "Water buffalo")')
*   [午](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E5%8D%88 "wikt:午"): [Old Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Chinese "Old Chinese") *[m].qʰˤaʔ (compare Proto-[Viet-Muong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietic_languages "Vietic languages") *m.ŋəːˀ)
*   [亥](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E4%BA%A5 "wikt:亥"): [Old Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Chinese "Old Chinese") *[g]ˤəʔ (compare Northern Proto-[Viet-Muong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietic_languages "Vietic languages") *kuːrˀ)

There is also a lexical correspondence with [Austronesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austronesian_languages "Austronesian languages"):[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-Ferlus2013-16)

*   [未](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%9C%AA "wikt:未"): [Old Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Chinese "Old Chinese") *m[ə]t-s (compare [Atayal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atayal_language "Atayal language") miːts)

The terms for the earthly branches are attested from [Shang dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shang_dynasty "Shang dynasty") inscriptions and were likely also used before Shang times. Ferlus (2013) suggests that the terms were ancient pre-Shang borrowings from Austroasiatic languages spoken in the Yangtze River region.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-Ferlus2013-16)

Within the [Four Pillars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Pillars_of_Destiny "Four Pillars of Destiny"), the year is the pillar representing information about the person's family background and society or relationship with their grandparents.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The person's age can also be easily deduced from their sign, the current sign of the year, and the person's generational disposition (teens, mid-20s, and so on). For example, a person born a [Tiger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiger_(zodiac) "Tiger (zodiac)") is 12, 24, 36, (etc.) years old in the year of the Tiger (2022); in the year of the [Rabbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabbit_(zodiac) "Rabbit (zodiac)") (2023), that person is one year older.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Different people born under each animal sign supposedly have different personalities, and practitioners of [Chinese astrology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_astrology "Chinese astrology") consult such [traditional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_culture "Chinese culture") details and compatibilities to offer putative guidance in life or for love and marriage.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-20) A common way to explore zodiac compatibility is with a chart showing how each zodiac sign interacts other signs. For example, constellations that are considered compatible with each other may have similar values and interests, while incompatible constellations may have conflicting personalities and ways of communicating.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-21)

## Origin stories

Many [stories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narrative "Narrative") and [fables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fable "Fable") explain the beginning of the [zodiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac "Zodiac"). Since the [Han dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_dynasty "Han dynasty"), the twelve [Earthly Branches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthly_Branches "Earthly Branches") have been used to record the time of day. However, for entertainment and convenience,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] they were replaced by the twelve animals, and a [mnemonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mnemonic "Mnemonic") refers to the behavior of the animals:

Earthly Branches may refer to a double-hour period.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-29) In the latter case it is the center of the period; for instance, 馬 mǎ ([Horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse_(zodiac) "Horse (zodiac)")) means noon as well as a period from 11:00 to 13:00.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Great Race

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chinese_zodiac&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Great Race")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/Rat_and_Ox.jpg/250px-Rat_and_Ox.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rat_and_Ox.jpg)

This image depicts a scene from "The Great Race" folk story, in which the [Ox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ox_(zodiac) "Ox (zodiac)") carries the [Rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rat_(zodiac) "Rat (zodiac)") across the river.

An ancient [folktale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folklore "Folklore")[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-30) called "The Great Race" tells of the [Jade Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jade_Emperor "Jade Emperor")'s decree that the years on the calendar would be named for each animal in the order they reached him. To get there, the animals would have to cross a river.

> The [Cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_(zodiac) "Cat (zodiac)") and the [Rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rat_(zodiac) "Rat (zodiac)") were not good at swimming, but they were both quite intelligent. They decided that the best and fastest way to cross the river was to hop on the back of the [Ox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ox_(zodiac) "Ox (zodiac)"). The Ox, being kindhearted and naive, agreed to carry them both across. As the Ox was about to reach the other side of the river, the Rat pushed the Cat into the water, and then jumped off the Ox and rushed to the Jade Emperor. It was named as the first animal of the zodiac calendar. The Ox had to settle for second place.
> 
> 
> The third animal to come was the [Tiger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiger_(zodiac) "Tiger (zodiac)"). Even though it was strong and powerful, it admitted to the Jade Emperor that the currents were pushing it downstream.
> 
> 
> Suddenly, a _thump_ sound came from the distance, signaling the arrival of the [Rabbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabbit_(zodiac) "Rabbit (zodiac)"). It explained how it crossed the river: by jumping from one stone to another in a nimble fashion. Halfway through, it thought it might lose the race, but it was lucky enough to grab hold of a floating log that later washed it to shore. For that, it became the fourth animal in the zodiac cycle.
> 
> 
> In fifth place was the flying [Dragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon_(zodiac) "Dragon (zodiac)"). The Jade Emperor wondered why a swift, airborne creature such as the Dragon did not come in first place. The Dragon explained that it had to stop by a village and bring rain for all the people, and therefore it was held back. Then, on its way to the finish, it saw the helpless Rabbit clinging onto a log, so it did a good deed and gave a puff of breath in the poor creature's direction so that it could land on the shore. The Jade Emperor was astonished by the Dragon's good nature, and it was named as the fifth animal of the zodiac.
> 
> 
> As soon as the Dragon arrived, there came a galloping sound, and the [Horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse_(zodiac) "Horse (zodiac)") appeared. Hidden on the Horse's hoof was the [Snake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake_(zodiac) "Snake (zodiac)"), whose sudden appearance gave the Horse a fright, thus making it fall back and giving the Snake the sixth spot while the Horse placed seventh.
> 
> 
> After a while, the [Goat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac) "Goat (zodiac)"), [Monkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monkey_(zodiac) "Monkey (zodiac)"), and [Rooster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rooster_(zodiac) "Rooster (zodiac)") came to the river blocking the heavenly gate. The Rooster found a raft, and the Monkey and the Goat tugged and pulled, trying to get all the weeds out of the way. With combined efforts, they managed to arrive to the other side. The Jade Emperor was pleased with their teamwork and decided to name the Goat as the eighth animal, followed by the Monkey and then the Rooster.
> 
> 
> The eleventh animal placed in the zodiac cycle was the [Dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog_(zodiac) "Dog (zodiac)"). Although it should have been the best swimmer and runner, it spent its time playing in the river water. Its explanation for being late was that it needed a good bath after a long journey, but it almost did not make it to the finish line.
> 
> 
> Right when the Jade Emperor was going to end the race, an _oink_ sound was heard: it was the [Pig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pig_(zodiac) "Pig (zodiac)"). The Pig felt hungry in the middle of the race, so it stopped, ate something, and then fell asleep. After it awoke, it finished the race in twelfth place, making it the last animal to arrive.
> 
> 
> The Cat eventually drowned and failed to become part of the zodiac. It is said that this is the reason why cats hate water. It is also the reason for the rivalry between the Cat and Rat, as it was the Rat's callous act to push the Cat into the river.

#### Variations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chinese_zodiac&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Variations")]

Another version of the folktale tells that the Rat deceived the Ox into letting it jump on its back by promising the Ox that it could hear the Rat sing,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-CyndiChen-31) before jumping off at the finish line and finishing first. Another variant says that the Rat cheated the Cat out its place at the finish line, by hiding on the back of the Dog, who was too focused to notice that he had a stow-away. The Cat tried to attack the rat in retaliation, but hurt the Dog by accident. This is said to account for the antagonistic dynamic between cats and rats, beyond normal predator and prey behavior, and also why dogs and cats fight.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In [Chinese mythology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_mythology "Chinese mythology"), a story tells that the cat was tricked by the Rat so it could not go to the banquet. This is why the Cat is ultimately not part of the Chinese zodiac.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In [Buddhist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Buddhism "Chinese Buddhism") legend [Gautama Buddha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gautama_Buddha "Gautama Buddha") summoned all animals of the [Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_(Wu_Xing) "Earth (Wu Xing)") to come before him before his departure from this [Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_(Wu_Xing) "Earth (Wu Xing)"), but only twelve animals came to bid him farewell. To reward these animals, he named a year after each of them in the order they had arrived.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac were developed in the early stages of [Chinese civilization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_China "History of China"), so therefore it is difficult to investigate its real origins. Most historians agree that the Cat is not included, as cats had not yet been introduced to China from India with the arrival of [Buddhism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism "Buddhism"). However until recently, the Vietnamese moved away from their [traditional texts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_Vietnamese_medicine "Traditional Vietnamese medicine")[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-32) and literature and, unlike all other countries who follow the Sino lunar calendar, include the Cat instead of the Rabbit as a zodiac animal. The most common explanation is that cats are worshipped by farmers in East Asia, believing that cats' luck and prosperity protects their crops.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-33) Another popular cultural reason is that the ancient word for [rabbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabbit_(zodiac) "Rabbit (zodiac)") (Mao) sounds like cat (Meo).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-34)

### The 36 Temporal Beasts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chinese_zodiac&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: The 36 Temporal Beasts")]

A variation of the double-hour system surfaced in the [Sui dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sui_dynasty "Sui dynasty"). A monk by the name of [Zhiyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhiyi "Zhiyi") (智顗) compiled a foundational text for the [Tiantai School of Buddhism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiantai "Tiantai"), and called it the [Mohe Zhiguan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohe_Zhiguan "Mohe Zhiguan") (摩訶止觀, _Great Calming and Contemplation_). In this text was a system called the **Thirty-Six Beasts** (三十六獸, _Sānshíliù Shòu_), also called the **Thirty-Six Animals** (三十六禽, _Sānshíliù Qín_) or **Thirty-Six Time Beasts** (三十六時獸).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac#cite_note-37)

The core shifting idea of this text was that each of the twelve earthly branches (the twelve two-hour periods of the day) was associated not with one animal, but with three; consequently, this meant there was a different animal associated with every 40-minute timespan throughout the day. Thus, the number of animals present was changed from 12 to 36 animals. The system was used in Buddhist meditation: these animals were thought to appear during different periods of the day to disturb the practitioner's concentration, and a specific spell (咒, _zhòu_) was prescribed to subdue them.

The list is organized by the twelve earthly branches and grouped into four sets of nine, each governed by one of the Four Elements (Wood, Fire, Metal, Water; Earth is excluded) and a cardinal direction. Each branch has three animals, corresponding to the morning (旦), midday (晝), and evening (暮) periods. There is no animal corresponding to midnight.

## Adaptations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chinese_zodiac&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Adaptations")]

The Chinese zodiac signs are also used by [cultures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_culture "Chinese culture") other than [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"). For example, they usually appear on [Korean New Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_New_Year "Korean New Year") and [Japanese New Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_New_Year "Japanese New Year")'s cards and stamps. The [United States Postal Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Postal_Service "United States Postal Service") and several other countries' postal services issue a "Year of the ____" postage stamp each year to honor this Chinese [heritage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_China "History of China").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The zodiac is widely used in commercial culture, for example, in the Chinese New Year market, and popular zodiac-related products, such as crafts, toys, books, accessories, and paintings and [Chinese lunar coins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_lunar_coins "Chinese lunar coins"). The coins depict [zodiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac "Zodiac") animals, inspired the [Canadian Silver Maple Leaf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Silver_Maple_Leaf#Privy_Mark_Silver_Maple_Leaf "Canadian Silver Maple Leaf")[coins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coin "Coin"), as well as varieties from [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia"), [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea"), and [Mongolia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongolia "Mongolia").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The Chinese zodiac is also used in some Asian countries that were under the [cultural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_culture "Chinese culture") influence of [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"). However, some of the animals in the [zodiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac "Zodiac") may differ by [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country "Country").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

# Meet X-Men Star You Didn't Know Was Kenyan

*   by [Marvin Chege](link_8) on Monday, 10 February 2020 - 12:00 pm 

Kenya is famous for numerous personalities who have flown the country’s flag high. From athletes like Eliud Kipchoge to football stars like Victor Wanyama to music personalities such as Sauti Sol who have set the entire continent alight with their music.

Little is, however, known of international actors who have made it on the international stage and were born in the country.Lupita Nyong’o the obvious name that comes to mind.The next should be X-Men star Edi Gathegi.

The Kenyan-American actor has been featured in several Hollywood films. He was born in 1979 in Umoja Estate, located in the Eastlands area of Nairobi County. He moved to the United States with his family to the city of Albany in California when he was just three years old.

He went to the University of California in Santa Barbara, California, USA where he played basketball. However, he suffered a knee injury which ended his basketball career.

This setback resulted in him taking acting classes and moving to New York University's Graduate Acting Program at the Tisch School of the Arts in 2002 and graduating in the year 2005.

The following year he scored his first major role, appearing alongside English actor Jason Statham and American actress Amy Smart in the 2006 action film _Crank_. He quickly earned roles alongside Hollywood aces Kevin Bacon in _Sentence_ and as character Cheese in Ben Affleck’s _Gone Baby Gone_.

He was not only gaining success in film, but he also was turning heads on television.

He appeared on _CSI: Miami,_ and earned much recognition and popularity for his recurring role as Dr. Jeffery “Big Love” Cole on _House M.D_. He also got a role in a popular TV show,_The Blacklist Season 3_, Mr. Solomon (Gathegi’s character) acting behalf of The Cabal, an alliance made up of some of the most powerful people in the world.

Other roles include _Kalume Ungara_ in an episode of _Nikita_, _Iggy_ as well as various characters in two episodes of animation series _Phineas and Ferb_ as well as _Jacobee_ in two episodes of _Into the Badlands_.

Gathegi’s career was gaining momentum and he received a suggestion from a casting director about auditioning for a role as a vampire in _The Twilight_ Saga.

He auditioned for the film and landed the role of _Laurent_ in the fantasy film. _Twilight_ became an international success and he retained his role for the franchise’s second film. He earned another high profile role as Armando Muñoz/Darwin in the Marvel Comics superhero film _X-Men: First Class._

Edi loves ugali as well as potatoes and is a fan of the Sauti Sol band. He spends his time travelling, playing sports, reading and watching movies, and prefers to spend his time in New York.

He is currently starring as Ronald Dacey, one of the main characters in the television drama series _StartUp._

| Born | Edi Mūe Gathegi[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-mue-1) (1979-03-10) March 10, 1979 (age 47) [Nairobi](link_0), [Nairobi City County](link_1), Kenya |
| Education | * [University of California, Santa Barbara](link_2)([BA](link_3)) * [New York University](link_4)([MFA](link_5)) |

**Edi Mūe Gathegi** ([/ˈ ɛ d i ˈ m w eɪ ɡ ə ˈ θ ɛ ɡ i/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English");[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] born March 10, 1979) is a [Kenyan-American](link_7) actor. He had his breakthrough playing Dr. Jeffrey "Big Love" Cole on the fourth season of the television series _[House](link_8)_ (2007), followed by his roles as Cheese in the 2007 film _[Gone Baby Gone](link_9)_, vampire [Laurent](link_10) in the films _[Twilight](link_11)_ and its sequel _[The Twilight Saga: New Moon](link_12)_, and as [Darwin](link_13) in _[X-Men: First Class](link_14)_. He played covert operative Matias Solomon on _[The Blacklist](link_15),_ which he reprised for the spinoff series _[The Blacklist: Redemption](link_16)_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-Spinoff-2)

Gathegi is also featured in the AMC series _[Into the Badlands](link_17)_ as Baron Jacobee. He has also played a leading role in _[Startup](link_18)_, a television drama series on [Crackle](link_19). Since 2022, Gathegi has played engineer and entrepreneur [Dev Ayesa](link_20) in the [Apple TV+](link_21) original [science fiction](link_22) space [drama](link_23) series _[For All Mankind](link_24)_, and played [Mister Terrific](link_25) in the [DC Universe](link_26) film _[Superman](link_27)_ (2025).

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edi_Gathegi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Born on March 10, 1979,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-3) in [Nairobi](link_0), [Kenya](link_6), Gathegi grew up in [Albany, California](link_28), U.S.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-vf-5) Gathegi attended the [University of California, Santa Barbara](link_2), where he played basketball until a knee injury ended his career. Gathegi then began taking acting classes.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-vf-5) He studied at [New York University](link_4)'s [Graduate Acting Program](link_29) at the [Tisch School of the Arts](link_29), graduating in 2005.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-6) Gathegi's career began in theatre,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-tl1-7) and his stage credits include _[Two Trains Running](link_30)_ at the [Old Globe Theatre](link_31), _[As You Like It](link_32)_, _[Twelfth Night](link_33)_, _[Othello](link_34)_, _[A Midsummer Night's Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Midsummer\_Night [link_35]'s\_Dream "A Midsummer Night's Dream")_, and _[Cyrano de Bergerac](link_36)_, among others.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-mue-1)

# News Tracker

### Sun, 04 October 2026

*   8:41 am **Presidential hopeful**Andrew Omtatah [restructures his Presidential Exploratory Committee,](link_6) appointing new leaders and extendin**g its tenure to November 2026.**
*   8:34 am **Lamu Port**recorded a major milestone after an **Iranian-flagged 366-metre container ship**docked at the facility, with more than **5,000 TEUs scheduled for discharge.**
*   7:14 am  A **wildfire**engulfed large [sections of Tsavo East National Park](link_7), with flames **spreading towards the Taveta-Voi highway** as the cause and response efforts remained unclear.

### Sat, 03 October 2026

*   7:50 pm A **Kenyan woman was among three rescued from a suspected prostitution**racket in India, where two hotel managers were arrested and investigations continued. 
*   6:57 pm **Kenya ranked 10th in Africa for average monthly net salary at Ksh44,553**, while Djibouti led with Ksh367,311, according to LiveGDP. 
*   6:38 pm [**Directline Assurance, the leading PSV insurer**](link_8) with a 62 per cent market share,**faces a liquidation petition by six creditors,**with hearings set for November 23. 
*   5:56 pm CAK approved **Mauritius-based Monarch Capital’s acquisition of a 60 per cent stake in De La Rue** Kenya, with the National Treasury retaining 40%. 

*   4:49 pm The Labour **Court has ruled supervisors can be dismissed for costly operational errors**, ordering a former bank team leader to repay Ksh9.78 million. 
*   3:55 pm Uhuru **Kenyatta warned Mt Kenya against repeating its 2022 political mistake,**dismissing claims he is an opposition “sponsor” and saying he seeks no office. 
*   3:20 pm Education CS Julius**Ogamba appointed new council members to six universities**, including Kenyatta University, Machakos University, JKUAT, and Dedan Kimathi University. 
*   2:47 pm **NCIC rejected reports clearing Kaluma and Otuoma,**saying their remarks were potentially threatening and ordering[corrective measures, including withdrawal, clarification, or conciliation.](link_9)
*   2:19 pm **Treasury’s reopened 15- and 20-year bonds attracted Ksh80.6 billion** in bids, surpassing the government’s Ksh50 billion target by 61.1 per cent, CBK says. 
*   1:56 pm Kenya**Met forecasts moderate to heavy rains in several counties,**including Nairobi, from October 4-8, [warning of thunderstorms and possible flooding.](link_10)
*   1:25 pm **NTSA warned motorists against dangerous overtaking** after a Salama crash killed 17 pilgrims, deploying [investigators to establish the accident’s circumstances.](link_11)
*   12:44 pm Kenya**Power warned customers against its hacked X account,** which posted cryptocurrency content, directing them to verified channels while recovery efforts continue. 
*   12:10 pm Three**suspects were arrested after police intercepted a petrol tanker** transporting 10,000 litres of suspected ethanol. 
*   11:57 am **IEK advised residents to vacate three Karibu Homes** blocks in Athi River after widening cracks raised concerns over foundation settlement and structural safety. 
*   11:44 am President **Ruto mourned 17 Catholic pilgrims killed in the Salama crash**, extending condolences to their families and wishing injured survivors a swift recovery. 
*   10:51 am **The Water****Tribunal ordered a site inspection after alleged demolitions continued in Nairobi West** despite an injunction protecting at least 50 families from eviction. 
*   9:39 am Kenyatta **University directed students to attend classes and exams despite a staff strike,** citing a court ruling declaring the planned action unprotected. 
*   8:49 am **Kenya and Türkiye agreed to expand health cooperation,** including specialist training and Uwezo Hospitals in six counties focused on maternal and paediatric care. 
*   8:31 am **Henry T. Wooster, a veteran diplomat** and former U.S. ambassador to Jordan, has been confirmed as [**the U.S. new ambassador to Kenya.**](link_12)
*   7:58 am At least **17 people died, and seven were injured after a lorry with suspected**brake failure rammed vehicles at [Salama along the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway.](link_13)
*   7:29 am A **pregnant woman died after allegedly being pushed from a moving police vehicle** by officers linked to Wang’uru Police Station, [prompting an IG-ordered DCI investigation.](link_14)

### Fri, 02 October 2026

*   6:30 pm **Bankers**call on **CBK** to retain the [Central Bank Rate (CBR) at 8.75 per cent](link_15) when the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** meets next week. 
*   6:00 pm **Raila Amolo Odinga**Mausoleum will be formally handed over to the state on **October 7**, ahead of a restricted dedication ceremony led by**President William Ruto**. 
*   5:30 pm **Detectives** raid **Githunguri premises** linked to suspected illegal cigarette trade, seize cigarettes and suspected fake **KRA excise stamps**. 
*   5:15 pm CS **Aden Duale**says the transition from the[**SHA** provider portal to the **HMIS**](link_16) aims to eliminate duplicate systems, reduce administrative work for hospitals, and improve **patient processing times**. 
*   5:00 pm **Lumakanda** OCS has been denied **bail** over allegations of defiling a**14-year-old child**, with the court citing the risk of **witness interference**.

_**Gone Baby Gone**_ is a 2007 American [crime drama](link_20) film directed by [Ben Affleck](link_1) in his directorial debut. Affleck co-wrote the screenplay with Aaron Stockard based on the [1998 novel of the same name](link_2) by [Dennis Lehane](link_3). The film stars [Casey Affleck](link_6) and [Michelle Monaghan](link_7) as two Boston private investigators hunting for a young girl abducted from her single mother's apartment in [Dorchester](link_21). The supporting cast includes [Morgan Freeman](link_8), [Ed Harris](link_9), and [Amy Ryan](link_11). It was the final film to be released by [The Ladd Company](link_18) before its closure on December 19, 2007.

Released by [Miramax Films](link_17) on October 19, 2007, _Gone Baby Gone_ was well-received by critics and grossed $34 million worldwide against a $19 million budget. Ben Affleck was lauded for his directing debut by critics, while Amy Ryan received an [Oscar](link_22) nomination for [Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress").

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gone_Baby_Gone&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In mid June 2006, in [Dorchester, Boston](link_21), [private investigator](link_23) Patrick Kenzie and his partner and girlfriend Angie Gennaro witness a televised plea by Helene McCready for the return of her abducted four-year-old daughter Amanda, who was last seen with her favorite doll, Mirabelle. Amid the media frenzy, Amanda's aunt Bea and uncle Lionel hire the pair to find her.

Patrick and Angie meet with [Boston Police Department](link_24) detectives Remy Bressant and Nick Poole, who tell them about Corwin Earle, a known [child molester](link_25) whom they consider a suspect. **Darwin** (**Armando Muñoz**) is a [mutant](link_10)[superhero](link_12) appearing in [American comic books](link_13) published by [Marvel Comics](link_4). The character was introduced in the series _[X-Men: Deadly Genesis](link_7)_, in which he was one of several previously unseen mutants recruited to rescue the original [X-Men](link_6) from [Krakoa](link_14). Darwin possesses the mutant ability of reactive evolution, which allows him to continuously transform his body to adapt to danger.

[Edi Gathegi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi "Edi Gathegi") portrays Darwin in the film _[X-Men: First Class](link_15)_.

## Publication history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Darwin_(character)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Publication history")]

Darwin first appeared in _[X-Men: Deadly Genesis](link_7)_ #2 (February 2006), and was created by writer [Ed Brubaker](link_8) and artist [Pete Woods](link_9).

## Fictional character biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Darwin_(character)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Fictional character biography")]

### Early life and Krakoa

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Darwin_(character)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early life and Krakoa")]

After birth, Darwin's powers of self-protection and continuous circumstantial [evolution](link_16) made his mother hate him. The Afro-Hispanic[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darwin_(character)#cite_note-1) boy was found by scientists who experimented on him, bringing him to the attention of the public. He was found by [Moira MacTaggert](link_17) and recruited as one of her "fosters". He was in the first team, along with [Kid Vulcan](link_18), [Petra](link_19), and [Sway](link_20) to attempt to rescue the [X-Men](link_6) from [Krakoa](link_14).

After Petra and Sway were killed by Krakoa, Darwin absorbed their remains and then converted himself into energy to fuse with Vulcan. This gave Vulcan the powers of Darwin, Petra, and Sway. [Rachel Summers](link_21) managed to expel Darwin's presence from Vulcan, who then took off for space. Years later, Vulcan is brought back to the Xavier Institute and Beast detects Darwin within him, having survived in an unconscious state. Once separated from Vulcan, Darwin's abilities restore his body.

### The Rise and Fall of the Shi'ar Empire

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Darwin_(character)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: The Rise and Fall of the Shi'ar Empire")]

When Professor X is abducted by [Shi'ar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shi [link_22]'ar "Shi'ar") agents, Darwin pursues them by secretly entering their spacecraft. Darwin succeeds in rescuing Xavier, but is captured by Shi'ar Imperium guards. Darwin is forced to be the best man at the wedding of Vulcan and [Deathbird](link_23), despite being opposed to their marriage, and attends the wedding in shackles. When the X-Men and [Starjammers](link_24) attack, Vulcan traps Xavier in the [M'Kraan Crystal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M [link_0]'Kraan_Crystal "M'Kraan Crystal") before Darwin frees him.

### World War Hulk

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Darwin_(character)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: World War Hulk")]

During the _[World War Hulk](link_25)_ storyline, Darwin is among the X-Men who battle the [Hulk](link_26). He attempts to absorb Hulk's [gamma radiation](link_27), but is unable to do so. Unable to confront Hulk directly, Darwin teleports several states away.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darwin_(character)#cite_note-World_War_Hulk-2)

### Secret Invasion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Darwin_(character)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Secret Invasion")]

Sometime after _[Messiah Complex](link_28)_, Darwin searches for Professor X and encounters [Longshot](link_29), who is unsure if his own powers have been working correctly. Longshot tests them out on a group of people, who turn on Darwin and attack. After a brief fight, Darwin escapes and the crowd turns on Longshot. Darwin later learns that this Longshot had been a [Skrull](link_30) imposter named Nogor.

### Joining X-Factor

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Darwin_(character)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Joining X-Factor")]

Darwin's father hires [X-Factor Investigations](link_11) to find him, supposedly because he feels bad for walking out on him and his mother when he was younger. After Darwin is reunited with his father, he is betrayed by him and sold to operatives of an organization known as the Karma Project. Their attempts to duplicate Darwin's powers fail when the duplicate Darwin's DNA proves incapable of handling his powers.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darwin_(character)#cite_note-3) Darwin is recruited into X-Factor, which allows him to deal with lesser threats than those faced by the X-Men.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darwin_(character)#cite_note-4)

During a battle with [Hela](link_31), Darwin adapts to her touch by becoming a death god himself, but has trouble coping with his abilities. He decides to leave the team to adjust and find himself.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darwin_(character)#cite_note-5)

_**Crank**_ is a 2006 American [action thriller film](link_16) written and directed by [Mark Neveldine and Brian Taylor](link_2) (in their directorial debut). It stars [Jason Statham](link_6), [Amy Smart](link_7), [Jose Pablo Cantillo](link_8), [Efren Ramirez](link_9) and [Dwight Yoakam](link_10). In the film, Chev Chelios (Statham), an [LA](link_17)–based American assassin, is poisoned by a synthetic drug and must keep his [adrenaline](link_18) flowing constantly to keep himself alive, while trying to track down the culprits responsible for poisoning him. It was followed by 2009 sequel; _[Crank: High Voltage](link_19)_.

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Crank_(film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

[L.A.](link_17)–based Englishman Chev Chelios works as a hitman under Don "Carlito" Carlos's crime empire. Chelios is contracted by Carlito to kill Don Kim, a mafia boss, because members of the [Triads](link_20) have been encroaching on Carlito's business. Ricky Verona, an ambitious small-time criminal, uses the opportunity to conspire with Carlito: Verona will kill Chelios so the Triads won't retaliate, then take Chelios's place as Carlito's newly hired gun.

Verona and his brother Alex break into Chelios' apartment, knock him out, and inject him with a Chinese [synthetic drug](link_21), dubbed the Beijing Cocktail, which inhibits the flow of [adrenaline](link_18), slowing the heart and eventually killing the victim. Chelios discovers what's been done and calls Doc Miles, a mafia surgeon. Miles informs him that to survive he must keep his adrenaline pumping and is unsure if the antidote exists.

Chelios keeps up his adrenaline through risky acts that elicit intense emotions, including picking fights with gangsters and police, reckless driving, taking illegal drugs, and having [public sex](link_22) with his girlfriend Eve. # Lupita's Emotional Tribute to 15-year-old Actress

*   by [Marvin Chege](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/by/marvin) on Monday, 17 February 2020 - 12:54 pm 

Kenyan-born award-winning actress Lupita Nyongo has penned her heartfelt condolences to Ugandan actress Nikita Pearl Waligwa, who played 'Gloria' in the Hollywood film _Queen of Katwe_.

Nikita passed away on Saturday, February 15, at the age of 15 at TMR International Hospital in Naalya, Kampala following a lengthy battle with brain cancer.

In her post on Instagram, Lupita described Nikita as a sweet, warm, talented girl whom she worked with on the film.

"It is with great sadness that I post about the passing of Nikita Waligwa, the sweet, warm, talented girl whom I worked with on the film, _Queen Of Katwe._ She played Gloria with such vibrancy," she began.

"In her real life, she had the enormous challenge of battling brain cancer. My thoughts and prayers are with her family and community as they come to terms with having to say goodbye so soon. May she truly rest in peace. May it be well with her soul," she concluded.

According to Ugandan media, Nikita Waligwa was first diagnosed with a brain tumour in 2016. She recovered a year later, only to be diagnosed with another brain tumour in early 2019.

Doctors then outlined that the tumour began at the sensitive part of her brain responsible for movement of limbs, speech and eyesight.

_Queen of Katwe_ is a 2016 Walt Disney biographical drama film and has been nominated for several awards.

The movie is a true story based on the life of Phiona Mutesi, a Ugandan girl residing in the slum of Katwe who began playing chess in the year 2005 and against all odds emerged as the first female winner in the Uganda junior chess championships.

By the age of 17, she was representing the country in international chess championships.

The news of her passing sparked a wave of condolences posted on social media by users who recalled the role she played in the movie filmed in Katwe, a slum in Uganda's capital, Kampala.

Nikita had a short but lively career as a stage, film and television performer.She will be laid to rest on Monday, February 17, in Kabojja, Wakiso District, in the Central Region of Uganda, according to Ugandan media reports.

**Efren Antonio Ramírez**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efren_Ramirez#cite_note-2) (born October 2, 1973)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efren_Ramirez#cite_note-Celeb_Bdays-1) is an American actor. He is best known for playing Pedro Sánchez in the 2004 indie film _[Napoleon Dynamite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon\_Dynamite "Napoleon Dynamite")_. He later reprised his role in the [2012 animated series of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon_Dynamite_(TV_series) "Napoleon Dynamite (TV series)").

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Efren_Ramirez&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Ramírez was born on October 2, 1973, in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), to [Salvadoran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvadorans "Salvadorans") parents. He has four brothers, one of whom is his identical twin Carlos.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efren_Ramirez#cite_note-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Efren_Ramirez&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Ramirez has starred in a number of films, including _Napoleon Dynamite_ as Pedro Sánchez, _[Employee of the Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Employee\_of\_the\_Month\_(2006\_film) "Employee of the Month (2006 film)")_, _[Crank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crank\_(film) "Crank (film)")_ and _[Crank: High Voltage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crank:\_High\_Voltage "Crank: High Voltage")_, _Searching for Mickey Fish_, _[All You've Got](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All\_You've\_Got "All You've Got")_, and _[Walkout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkout\_(film) "Walkout (film)")_ and made cameos in _[Nacho Libre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nacho\_Libre "Nacho Libre")_ and _[Mr. & Mrs. Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_&\_Mrs.\_Smith\_(2005\_film) "Mr. & Mrs. Smith (2005 film)")_. In 2011, Efren starred in the comedy _[American Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Summer\_(2008\_film) "American Summer (2008 film)")_ as well as appearing as a contestant on MTV's _[Celebrity Rap Superstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity\_Rap\_Superstar "Celebrity Rap Superstar")_. On July 14, 2008 [Sierra Mist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Mist "Sierra Mist") released a series of commercials aimed at multicultural consumers in which Efren stars.

Soon after the success of _Napoleon Dynamite_, the music group [G. Love and Special Sauce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G._Love_and_Special_Sauce "G. Love and Special Sauce") asked Efren to appear in their music video "Booty Call". He also played [Ashlee Simpson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashlee_Simpson "Ashlee Simpson")'s boyfriend in the music video for her 2005 song "[Boyfriend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boyfriend_(Ashlee_Simpson_song) "Boyfriend (Ashlee Simpson song)")". Ramírez made a cameo appearance in a 2005 episode of [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company")'s _[George López](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George\_Lopez\_(TV\_series) "George Lopez (TV series)")_ wearing a T-shirt similar to the shirt [Jon Heder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Heder "Jon Heder") wears in _Napoleon Dynamite_ that reads, "Vote For Pedro". In 2007 Ramírez appeared as the judge for an acting challenge on [Cycle 8 of _America's Next Top Model_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Next_Top_Model,_Cycle_8 "America's Next Top Model, Cycle 8").

Ramírez made several cameos throughout his career. In [_King Cobra_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Cobra_(1999_film) "King Cobra (1999 film)"), he portrayed a teenager playing a game of [hide-and-seek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hide-and-seek "Hide-and-seek") with his girlfriend (portrayed by Ramirez's wife [Iyari Limon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iyari_Limon "Iyari Limon")). They later end up as prey for the title [antagonist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antagonist "Antagonist"). In the music video for [Sleazy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleazy_(Kesha_song) "Sleazy (Kesha song)"), Pedro appears as a cameo and lip syncs [André 3000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9_3000 "André 3000")'s verse.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efren_Ramirez#cite_note-4)

He co-founded Powerhouse Pictures Entertainment, LLC with [Chris Barrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Barrett_(filmmaker) "Chris Barrett (filmmaker)"), and they co-authored the book _Direct Your Own Life: How To Be A Star in Any Field You Choose_ being published on June 10, 2008 through [Kaplan Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaplan_Publishing "Kaplan Publishing").

**John David Ashton** (February 22, 1948 – September 26, 2024) was an American actor, known for his roles in the _[Beverly Hills Cop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly\_Hills\_Cop\_(franchise) "Beverly Hills Cop (franchise)")_ films, _[Some Kind of Wonderful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Some\_Kind\_of\_Wonderful\_(film) "Some Kind of Wonderful (film)")_, and _[Midnight Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight\_Run "Midnight Run")_.

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Ashton_(actor)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Born in [Springfield, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springfield,_Massachusetts "Springfield, Massachusetts"), Ashton attended [Defiance College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defiance_College "Defiance College") in Ohio and was a graduate of the [University of Southern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_California "University of Southern California") School of Theatre and Dance.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Ashton_(actor)#cite_note-Buchanan-1) He attended [Enfield High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enfield_High_School "Enfield High School") in [Enfield, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enfield,_Connecticut "Enfield, Connecticut").

Ashton made numerous appearances in both television and feature films. He played Willie Joe Garr on several episodes of _[Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas\_(TV\_series) "Dallas (TV series)")_. He appeared in an episode of _[Columbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List\_of\_Columbo\_episodes#Season\_4 "List of Columbo episodes")_, "Negative Reaction", and in episode 5 of _[Police Squad!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police\_Squad! "Police Squad!")_, "Rendezvous at Big Gulch (Terror in the Neighborhood)".

His early film credits included roles in _[An Eye for an Eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Psychopath\_(1973\_film) "The Psychopath (1973 film)")_ (1973), _[Breaking Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breaking\_Away "Breaking Away")_ (1979), _[Borderline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borderline\_(1980\_film) "Borderline (1980 film)")_ (1980), _[Honky Tonk Freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honky\_Tonk\_Freeway "Honky Tonk Freeway")_ (1981), _[Last Resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last\_Resort\_(1986\_film) "Last Resort (1986 film)")_ (1986) and _[King Kong Lives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Kong\_Lives "King Kong Lives")_ (1986).

Ashton starred as Detective Sergeant John Taggart in the first two installments of the _[Beverly Hills Cop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly\_Hills\_Cop\_(franchise) "Beverly Hills Cop (franchise)")_ series, alongside [Eddie Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Murphy "Eddie Murphy") and [Judge Reinhold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judge_Reinhold "Judge Reinhold"). He appeared as [Eric Stoltz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Stoltz "Eric Stoltz")'s character's father in the 1987 [John Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hughes_(filmmaker) "John Hughes (filmmaker)")-penned comedy-drama _[Some Kind of Wonderful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Some\_Kind\_of\_Wonderful\_(film) "Some Kind of Wonderful (film)")_, and worked with Hughes again in _[She's Having a Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She's\_Having\_a\_Baby "She's Having a Baby")_ in 1988.

In 1988, he co-starred in the action-comedy _[Midnight Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight\_Run "Midnight Run")_ as a rival bounty hunter to [Robert De Niro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_De_Niro "Robert De Niro")'s character. He starred in _[Little Big League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little\_Big\_League "Little Big League")_ (1994) with Luke Edwards, _[Trapped in Paradise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trapped\_in\_Paradise "Trapped in Paradise")_ (1994), _[The Shooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Shooter\_(1995\_film) "The Shooter (1995 film)")_ (1995), _[Meet the Deedles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet\_the\_Deedles "Meet the Deedles")_ (1998), _[Instinct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instinct\_(1999\_film) "Instinct (1999 film)")_ (1999), and appeared in a supporting role in the 2007 drama _[Gone Baby Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone\_Baby\_Gone "Gone Baby Gone")_ directed by [Ben Affleck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck "Ben Affleck").
