Morgan Freeman[2] (born June 1, 1937) is an American actor, producer, and narrator. In a career spanning six decades, he has received numerous accolades, including an Academy Award and a Golden Globe Award, as well as a nomination for a Grammy Award and a Tony Award. He was honored with the Kennedy Center Honor in 2008, an AFI Life Achievement Award in 2011, the Cecil B. DeMille Award in 2012, and Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award in 2018. In a 2022 readers' poll by Empire, he was voted one of the 50 greatest actors of all time.[3]

Born in Memphis, Tennessee, Freeman was raised in Mississippi, where he began acting in school plays. He studied theater arts in Los Angeles and appeared in stage productions in his early career. He rose to fame in the 1970s for his role in the children's television series The Electric Company. Freeman then appeared in the Shakespearean plays Coriolanus and Julius Caesar, the former of which earned him an Obie Award. In 1978, he was nominated for the Tony Award for Best Featured Actor in a Play for his role as Zeke in the Richard Wesley play The Mighty Gents.

Freeman received the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor playing a former boxer in Clint Eastwood's sports drama Million Dollar Baby (2004). He was Oscar-nominated for Street Smart (1987), Driving Miss Daisy (1989), The Shawshank Redemption (1994), and Invictus (2009). He also performed in Glory (1989), Lean on Me (1989), Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves (1991), Unforgiven (1992), Se7en (1995), Amistad (1997), Deep Impact (1998), Gone Baby Gone (2007), and The Bucket List (2007). He also portrayed Lucius Fox in Christopher Nolan's Dark Knight trilogy (2005–2012) and acted in the action films Wanted (2008), Red (2010), Oblivion (2013), the Now You See Me films (2013–2025), and Lucy (2014).

Known for his distinctive voice, he has narrated numerous documentaries including The Long Way Home (1997), March of the Penguins (2005), Through the Wormhole (2010–2017), The Story of God with Morgan Freeman (2016–2019), Our Universe (2022) and Life on Our Planet (2023). He made his directorial debut with the drama Bopha! (1993). He founded the film production company Revelations Entertainment with business partner Lori McCreary in 1996, under which they produced projects such as the CBS political drama Madam Secretary (2014–2019).

Early life and education

Freeman was born on June 1, 1937, in Memphis, Tennessee.[4] He is the son of Mamie Edna (née Revere; 1912–2000), a teacher,[5] and Morgan Porterfield Freeman (July 6, 1915 – April 27, 1961),[2] a barber, who died of cirrhosis in 1961.[6] He has three older siblings.[7] Some of Morgan's great-great-grandparents were slaves who migrated from North Carolina to Mississippi. He later discovered that his white maternal great-great-grandfather had lived with and was buried beside Freeman's black great-great-grandmother in the segregated South, as the two could not legally marry at the time.[5] A DNA test suggested that among all of his African ancestors, a little over one-quarter came from the area that stretches from present-day Senegal to Liberia and three-quarters came from the Congo-Angola region.[8]

As an infant, Freeman was sent to his paternal grandmother in Charleston, Mississippi.[9][10] He moved frequently during his childhood, living in Greenwood, Mississippi, Gary, Indiana, and finally Chicago.[10] He made his acting debut aged nine, playing the lead role in a school play. He then attended Broad Street High School, a building which serves today as Threadgill Elementary School in Greenwood.[11] At the age of 12, he won a statewide drama competition, and while settling into school, discovered music and theater. When Freeman was 16 years old, he contracted pneumonia.[12]

Freeman graduated from high school in 1955, but turned down a partial drama scholarship from Jackson State University, opting instead to enlist in the United States Air Force.[6] He served as an Automatic Tracking Radar repairman, rising to the rank of airman first class.[13] After serving from 1955 to 1959, he moved to Los Angeles and took acting classes at the Pasadena Playhouse.[6] He also studied theater arts at Los Angeles City College, where a teacher encouraged him to embark on a dance career.[14]

Career
1964–1988: Early work and rise to prominence

Freeman worked as a dancer at the 1964 World's Fair and was a member of the Opera Ring musical theater group in San Francisco.[15] He acted in a touring company version of The Royal Hunt of the Sun, and also appeared as an extra in Sidney Lumet's 1965 drama film The Pawnbroker starring Rod Steiger.[15] Between acting and dancing jobs, Freeman realized that acting was where his heart lay. "After The Royal Hunt of the Sun, my acting career just took off", he later recalled.[15] Freeman made his Off-Broadway debut in 1967, opposite Viveca Lindfors in The Niggerlovers, a show about the Freedom Riders during the American Civil Rights Movement,[16] before debuting on Broadway in 1968's all-black version of Hello, Dolly! that also starred Pearl Bailey and Cab Calloway.[17] In 1969, Freeman also performed on stage in The Dozens.[18]

Beginning in 1971, Freeman starred in the PBS children's television show The Electric Company, which gave him financial stability and recognition among American audiences.[10] His work on the show was tiring, so he quit in 1975.[14] Television producer Joan Ganz Cooney said that Freeman loathed appearing in The Electric Company, saying "it was a very unhappy period in his life".[19] Freeman later acknowledged that he does not think about the show, but he was grateful to have been a part of it.[20] His first credited appearance in a feature film was in 1971's Who Says I Can't Ride a Rainbow!, a family drama starring Jack Klugman.[18] Also that year, Freeman performed in a theater production of Purlie.[21] After a short career break, he returned to work in 1978, appearing in two stage productions: 1978's The Mighty Gents, winning a Drama Desk Award and a Clarence Derwent Award for his role as a wino,[22] and White Pelicans.[23] Freeman continued to work in theater and a year later, appeared in the Shakespearean tragedies Coriolanus, receiving the Obie Award in 1980 for the title role[15] as well as Julius Caesar.[24]

In 1980, he had a small role as Walter in the drama Brubaker, which starred Robert Redford as a prison warden.[25] Freeman next appeared in the television film, Attica (1980), which is about the 1971 Attica Prison riot and its aftermath.[26] A year later he had a lead role in Peter Yates' Eyewitness with co-stars William Hurt and Sigourney Weaver.[27] From 1982 to 1984, Freeman was a cast member of the soap opera Another World, playing architect Roy Bingham.[28] After several small roles in dramas, he starred in Marie (1985), a film adaptation of Marie: A True Story by Peter Maas; he portrayed Charles Traughber.[29] He also appeared in the miniseries The Atlanta Child Murders.[30] Freeman also had a small role in the drama That Was Then... This Is Now, based on the novel of the same name by S. E. Hinton.[31] In the mid-1980s, he began accepting prominent supporting roles in feature films, earning him a reputation for depicting wise, fatherly characters.[10]

In addition to television films, in 1987, Freeman played a violent street hustler, a role that diverged from his previous roles, in Street Smart co-starring Christopher Reeve and Kathy Baker. Freeman's performance was praised by film critics, including Roger Ebert who wrote: "Freeman has the flashier role, as a smart, very tough man who can be charming or intimidating-whatever's needed ... Freeman creates such an unforgettable villain."[32] Freeman's performance earned him an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor.[33] He later said that he considered Street Smart to be his breakthrough role.[20] In his next film, he played Craig in the drama Clean and Sober with co-stars Michael Keaton and Kathy Baker. Although the film was not a box-office hit, it gained fair reviews; Roger Ebert gave the film 31⁄2 out of 4 stars and called the performances "superb".[34] Freeman also received Obie Awards for his roles as a preacher in the musical The Gospel at Colonus, and as Hoke Colburn in the play Driving Miss Daisy, respectively.[15]

1989–1996: Hollywood breakthrough
Freeman in 1998

Freeman had four film releases in 1989. In the first, he starred as Sergeant Major John Rawlins in Glory, directed by Edward Zwick, about the 54th Massachusetts Infantry Regiment, the Union Army's second African-American regiment in the American Civil War. Writing for The Washington Post, Desson Thomson praised Freeman and co-star Denzel Washington for their "warming sense of fraternity".[35] Glory was nominated for five Academy Awards and won three: Best Supporting Actor for Washington, Best Cinematography, and Best Sound.[36] Next, Freeman starred in the comedy-drama Driving Miss Daisy, alongside Jessica Tandy and Dan Aykroyd. Based on Alfred Uhry's play of the same name in which Freeman had appeared previously, he reprises his role of Hoke Colburn, chauffeur for a Jewish widow. The film was a commercial success and grossed US$145 million worldwide.[37] Film critics were mainly positive; Henry Sheehan from The Hollywood Reporter opined that Freeman and Tandy's performances complemented each other while retaining their "individual star-quality".[38] The film was nominated for nine Academy Awards (and received four, Best Picture being one of them), including Best Actor for Freeman.[36]

His third release was the biographical drama Lean on Me, in which he portrays the principal of an under-performing and drug- and crime-ridden New Jersey high school. Jane Galbraith of Variety magazine thought Freeman's casting was "wonderful".[39] Lastly in 1989, he starred in Walter Hill's Johnny Handsome, a crime drama in which he plays a New Orleans police officer.[40] In a 1990 interview, Freeman said that Glory was one of his favorite releases—"The Black legacy is as noble, is as heroic, is as filled with adventure and conquest and discovery as anybody else's. It's just that nobody knows it."[14] In 1990, Freeman provided the voice of Frederick Douglass in The Civil War, a television miniseries about the American Civil War.[41] In the same year he played a key role in the critically panned The Bonfire of the Vanities. According to the review aggregate site Rotten Tomatoes, the film has an approval rating of 16% based on 51 reviews.[42] In the summer of 1990, he played Petruchio, a role he had been thinking about for six years, in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew, which opened at Delacorte theater in New York City. "[Petruchio] seems to have a lot of fun in life", he said.[43] In 1991, Freeman had a supporting role in Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves, an action-adventure starring Kevin Costner. The film was a commercial success,[44] but garnered mixed reviews from critics; The New York Times' Vincent Canby thought Freeman played Azeem with "wit and humor" despite the "muddled" plot.[45]

Freeman at the 62nd Academy Awards in 1990

Freeman also narrated The True Story of Glory Continues, a documentary about the 54th Massachusetts Infantry Regiment.[46] In 1992, he appeared in Clint Eastwood's western Unforgiven, which won four Academy Awards including Best Picture.[47] The film depicts William Munny (Eastwood), an aging outlaw and killer who takes on one more job with old friend Ned Logan (Freeman). Unforgiven was widely acclaimed, with one critic calling Freeman's performance "outstanding".[48] Also in 1992 Freeman starred in the John G. Avildsen directed drama The Power of One acting opposite Stephen Dorf and John Gielgud in a loose adaptation of Bryce Courtenay's 1989 novel of the same name, in which he plays boxing coach Geel Piet.[49] In 1993, Freeman made his directorial debut with the drama Bopha!, which tells the story of a black policeman (Danny Glover) during South Africa's apartheid era. Bopha! was well-received, in particular for Freeman's directing. Hal Hinson of The Washington Post wrote: "Freeman lays out the father-son dynamics with great skill and very little fuss. There's no hysteria in his approach; instead, he sticks to the facts, relying on his cast to provide the emotion. The result is a surprisingly powerful, insightful film."[50] Kenneth Turan from Los Angeles Times also complimented Freeman's direction but thought the film was "more predictable than powerful".[51]

In 1994, Freeman portrayed Red, the redeemed convict in Frank Darabont's acclaimed drama The Shawshank Redemption, with co-star Tim Robbins. It is based on the 1982 Stephen King novella Rita Hayworth and the Shawshank Redemption. Freeman was cast at the suggestion of producer Liz Glotzer, despite the novella's character of a white Irishman.[52] Filming proved to be challenging, mainly because of Darabont's need for multiple takes. Freeman said, "The answer [I'd give him] was no ... having to do something again and again for no discernible reason tends to be a bit debilitating to the energy."[52] Nevertheless, his performance was described as "quietly impressive" and "moving" by The New York Times.[53] At the 67th Academy Awards the film received Academy Award nominations for Best Picture and a nomination for Freeman for Best Actor losing to Tom Hanks in Forrest Gump (1994).[54] Since its release, The Shawshank Redemption has remained popular among audiences.[52] In 1994, Freeman served as a member of the jury at the 44th Berlin International Film Festival.[55]

Outbreak (1995), a medical thriller directed by Wolfgang Petersen, was Freeman's next film. He played General Billy Ford, a doctor dealing with an outbreak of a fictional virus in a small town. The film stars Dustin Hoffman, Rene Russo, and Donald Sutherland. Outbreak was a box-office success, grossing $189.8 million worldwide,[56] but gained a mixed critics' response.[57] Mick LaSelle of the San Francisco Chronicle credited Freeman for his performance which may have been unappreciated by viewers.[58] In 1995, Freeman starred with Brad Pitt in David Fincher's crime thriller Seven, the story of two detectives who attempt to identify a serial killer who bases his murders on the Christian seven deadly sins. Freeman's performance generated a positive response; Owen Gleiberman of Entertainment Weekly wrote: "Freeman plays nearly every scene in a doleful hush; he makes you lean in to hear his words, to ferret out the hints of anger and regret that haunt this weary knight."[59] The critic from Variety magazine called Freeman's acting "supremely nuanced".[60]

While filming Outbreak, Freeman expressed an interest in starting a film production company. He turned to McCreary, the producer of Bopha!, to be his business partner. Freeman explained that he wanted to achieve representation on screen, explore challenging issues and reveal hidden truths, so they chose to name their firm Revelations Entertainment.[61] A year later, he appeared in Chain Reaction as Paul Shannon, a science-fiction thriller co-starring Keanu Reeves and Rachel Weisz. The film was a critical and commercial disappointment.[62][63] Next, he was cast opposite Robin Wright in 1996's Moll Flanders, a period drama based on the novel of the same name. The film received a mixed reception; Greg Evans from Variety magazine said Freeman gave a "sweet" performance,[64] while The New York Times critic thought he was miscast.[65]

1997–2004: Critical success and established actor
Freeman in 1998

In 1997, Freeman narrated the Academy Award-winning documentary The Long Way Home, about Jewish refugees' liberation after World War II and the establishment of Israel.[23] He also appeared in Steven Spielberg's historical epic Amistad alongside Djimon Hounsou, Anthony Hopkins, and Matthew McConaughey. Based on the events in 1839 aboard the slave ship La Amistad, the film was mostly well-received and earned four nominations at the Academy Awards.[66][67] The critic from Salon magazine, however, thought the film lacked inspiration and Freeman's role was "utterly cryptic".[68] In that same year, he was cast as psychologist Alex Cross in Kiss the Girls, a thriller based on James Patterson's 1995 novel of the same name. In a mixed review, Peter Stack of San Francisco Chronicle thought Freeman and co-star Ashley Judd gave strong performances despite the lengthy plot.[69]

Freeman went on to star in Deep Impact (1998), a science-fiction disaster film in which he played President Tim Beck.[70] The story depicts humanity's attempt to destroy a 7-mile (11 km) wide comet set to collide with Earth and cause a mass extinction. The film was a box-office hit, despite competition from Armageddon, another summer blockbuster of the year.[71] Continuing with the disaster genre, he then starred opposite Christian Slater in 1998's Hard Rain, centering on a heist and man-made treachery amidst a natural disaster in a small Indiana town. The film was unpopular with critics; Lawrence Van Gelder of The New York Times called the characters "one-dimensional" and the film "routine".[72] Freeman returned to the screen in 2000 with the lead role of Charlie in the comedy Nurse Betty, featuring Renée Zellweger, Chris Rock, and Greg Kinnear. The film premiered at the Cannes Film Festival to mainly positive reviews; the critic from Variety magazine thought Freeman and Rock had "wonderful chemistry".[73] Next, he appeared in Under Suspicion (2000), a thriller remake of the 1981 French film Garde à vue. The film had been "carting round" for twelve years before Freeman was able to produce it under Revelations Entertainment.[74] He co-starred with Gene Hackman; "Working with Gene was wonderful. I didn't find it too hard working with an icon I so respected", Freeman said.[74] Upon release, Under Suspicion was met with lukewarm reception;[75] CNN's Paul Ta

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

American filmmaking duo

| Mark Neveldine and Brian Taylor |
| --- |
| Born | [Mark Neveldine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Neveldine "Mark Neveldine") (1973-05-11) May 11, 1973 (age 53) [Watertown, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watertown_(city),_New_York "Watertown (city), New York"), United States * * * [Brian Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Taylor_(filmmaker) "Brian Taylor (filmmaker)") United States |
| Other names | * Neveldine/Taylor * Neveldine & Taylor |
| Occupations | Film directors, producers screenwriters, [cinematographers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematographer "Cinematographer"), [camera operators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camera_operator "Camera operator") |
| Years active | 2006–2011 (as a duo) |

**[Mark Neveldine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Neveldine "Mark Neveldine") and [Brian Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Taylor_(filmmaker) "Brian Taylor (filmmaker)")** are two American filmmakers who formerly collaborated as a filmmaking duo. They are sometimes referred to as **Neveldine & Taylor** or **Neveldine/Taylor**. Their written and directed productions are known for being dark, edgy, bizarre, and over-the-top, while maintaining a small budget. Both Neveldine and Taylor have written and directed several films together that include _[Crank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crank\_(film) "Crank (film)")_ and its sequel, _[Crank: High Voltage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crank:\_High\_Voltage "Crank: High Voltage")_.

## Films

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Neveldine_and_Brian_Taylor&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Films")]

[Mark Neveldine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Neveldine "Mark Neveldine") and [Brian Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Taylor_(filmmaker) "Brian Taylor (filmmaker)") made their feature film debut with _[Crank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crank\_(film) "Crank (film)")_, a 2006 film starring [Jason Statham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Statham "Jason Statham"). The duo later wrote and produced the 2008 thriller _[Pathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathology\_(film) "Pathology (film)")_. In 2009, Neveldine and Taylor wrote and directed _[Crank: High Voltage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crank:\_High\_Voltage "Crank: High Voltage")_, a sequel to _Crank_, and _[Gamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamer\_(2009\_film) "Gamer (2009 film)")_, a science fiction action thriller starring [Gerard Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Butler "Gerard Butler"). The duo were originally slated to direct the [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonah_Hex_(film) "Jonah Hex (film)") of [DC Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Comics "DC Comics")'s _[Jonah Hex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonah\_Hex "Jonah Hex")_, but stepped down due to creative differences with film distributor [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") They are still credited as screenwriters for the film.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Neveldine_and_Brian_Taylor#cite_note-Jonah_Hex_loses_directors-1) The duo directed _[Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost\_Rider:\_Spirit\_of\_Vengeance "Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance")_ (2011), the [sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequel "Sequel") to _[Ghost Rider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost\_Rider\_(2007\_film) "Ghost Rider (2007 film)")_.

### Cinematography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Neveldine_and_Brian_Taylor&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Cinematography")]

Neveldine and Taylor frequently serve as [camera operators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camera_operator "Camera operator") for their films, and are known for having their films shot entirely in [high-definition video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-definition_video "High-definition video"). As camera operators, the duo are known for their "roller dolly" technique, which involves the camera shooting the film while on rollerblades. Taylor commented on this technique while filming _Crank_: "The Rollercam footage was really the most dramatic and technically challenging of the movie. Mark absolutely could not be tethered or restricted by any cables when blading at speeds up to 30mph..."[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Neveldine_and_Brian_Taylor#cite_note-Sony-2)

For _Crank: High Voltage_, the duo used consumer-grade camcorders, such as the [Canon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canon_(company) "Canon (company)") HF10 and the Canon XH-A1. Neveldine commented on the use of these cameras: "We can put these cameras in places that people haven’t and we can put 10 of them in places where people haven't...And one of the things it allows us to do is we're doing this moving bullet time camera rig where we take 8 HF-10s and we put it on a light weight piece of speed rail and I can roller blade and skate around Jason Statham as he’s blasting down the street with a weapon and capture just rad images."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Neveldine_and_Brian_Taylor#cite_note-First_Look-3) During the filming of _Crank: High Voltage_, Neveldine and Taylor shot over 279 hours of footage during its 31 days of production.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Neveldine_and_Brian_Taylor#cite_note-SlashFilm1-4)

Neveldine and Taylor's third directorial effort, _Gamer_ was the second feature film (following _[Che](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Che\_(2008\_film) "Che (2008 film)")_) to be shot with special hand-held [Red One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Digital_Cinema_Camera_Company "Red Digital Cinema Camera Company") digital cameras.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Neveldine_and_Brian_Taylor#cite_note-Gerard_Butler's_New_Sci-Fi_flick-5)

# Facts

*   ![Image 2: The inside of an elevator fitted with mirrors.](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/files/styles/article_300x150/public/images/media/elevator.jpg.webp?itok=gCs5IiIq)   Sat, 26 Sep 2026 - 12:02 pm by Timothy Cerullo 
## [Little-Known Reasons Why Lifts Have Mirrors Inside Them](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/news/127367-explainer-why-many-lifts-are-fitted-mirrors)​​

The mirrors are strategically fitted across lift walls, leaving many wondering why they are installed and what purpose they actually serve.     
*   ![Image 3: a collage of the BCG Vaccine mark at birth and after several years](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/files/styles/article_300x150/public/images/media/bcg-vaccine-scar.jpg.webp?itok=SZS8EHVs)   Sun, 20 Sep 2026 - 6:11 pm by Joseph Ogungo 
## [Explained: Why the BCG Vaccine Leaves a Permanent Mark on Your Arm](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/news/127024-explained-why-bcg-vaccine-leaves-permanent-scar)​​

To some, the scar remains even into old age, while in some people, it disappears after vaccination.   
*   ![Image 4: kdf-blades-rifles.jpg](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/files/styles/article_300x150/public/images/media/kdf-blades-rifles.jpg.webp?itok=EiTh7tru)   Sat, 12 Sep 2026 - 1:08 pm by Frankline Oduor 
## [Why KDF Attach Blades to Guns During Parades](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/news/126994-why-military-and-police-attach-blades-guns-during-parades)​​

The attachment of blades is a common practice around the world and has roots deep in historical times.      
*   ![Image 5: plane-jet.jpg](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/files/styles/article_300x150/public/images/media/plane-jet.jpg.webp?itok=IJKjit6a)   Sat, 15 Aug 2026 - 7:57 pm by Frankline Oduor 
## [Explained: Why Passenger Plane Noses Are Rounded While Fighter Jets Have Pointed Noses](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/news/126214-explained-why-passenger-plane-noses-are-rounded-while-fighter-jets-have-pointed-noses)​​

Engineers often have to decide on a specific design for key features of planes and jets, usually based on the functions the aircraft would be used for.   
*   ![Image 6: kdf-police-vehicle.](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/files/styles/article_300x150/public/images/media/kdf-police-vehicle.jpg.webp?itok=8jxY0bSX)   Sun, 26 Jul 2026 - 5:19 pm by Frankline Oduor 
## [Explained: Why KDF Soldiers Face Outward on Military Trucks While Police Face Inward](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/news/125607-explained-why-kdf-soldiers-sit-facing-outward-military-trucks-unlike-police-officers)​​

Military officers are often seated in full combat gear, carrying rifles in a ready position while constantly scanning their surroundings as they move.  
*   ![Image 7: Moja Expressway Company](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/files/styles/article_300x150/public/images/media/mtc-etc-markings-on-nairobi-expressway.jpg.webp?itok=QxvbvPn6)   Sun, 19 Jul 2026 - 7:32 pm by Maxwell Amunga 
## [Meaning of ETC, MTC, and Other Markings on Nairobi Expressway](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/news/125417-meaning-etc-mtc-and-other-markings-nairobi-expressway)​​

To comfortably use the Nairobi Expressway, one has to fully understand the meanings behind the various markings on the various entrance and exit points of the 27.1-Kilometer highway.  
*   ![Image 8: Most Rev. Dominic Kimengich](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/files/styles/article_300x150/public/images/media/catholic.jpg.webp?h=8be7c3c4&itok=5jUkG09R)   Sat, 9 May 2026 - 6:11 pm by Frankline Oduor 
## [Explained: Why Catholic Bishops Wear Small Caps and Other Religious Attire](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/news/123242-explained-why-catholic-bishops-wear-small-caps-and-other-religious-attire)​​

The vestments are not just for fashion but rather have deep spiritual reflection that dates back to the early history of the church, which has remained nearly the same over time.      
*   ![Image 9: A man carrying a bale of imported second-hand clothes, commonly referred to as Mitumba, at the Port of Mombasa.](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/files/styles/article_300x150/public/images/media/mitumba.jpg.webp?h=98fd8cef&itok=x5sh32sS)   Thu, 7 May 2026 - 6:59 pm by Frankline Oduor 
## [Finance Bill 2026: How New Mitumba Taxes Will Work](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/news/123209-finance-bill-2026-how-new-mitumba-taxes-will-work)​​

There have been concerns that the new tax proposals could push up the prices of popular second-hand clothing and potentially discourage its uptake among consumers.    
*   ![Image 10: An image of Matatus in the busy streets of Nairobi, with a fuel pump with fuel drop on the side.](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/files/styles/article_300x150/public/images/media/fuel-drop-matatus.jpg.webp?itok=5ojh3jat)   Fri, 1 May 2026 - 11:42 am by Nikkie Aisha

**Amy Beth Dziewiontkowski** (born May 3, 1968),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Ryan#cite_note-1) known professionally as **Amy Ryan**, is an American actress. She began her professional stage career in 1987 and made her [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") debut in 1993 as a replacement in the original production of [Wendy Wasserstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Wasserstein "Wendy Wasserstein")'s _[The Sisters Rosensweig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sisters\_Rosensweig "The Sisters Rosensweig")_. She was nominated for the [Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Featured_Actress_in_a_Play "Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Play") for her performances in _[Uncle Vanya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncle\_Vanya "Uncle Vanya")_ (2000) and _[A Streetcar Named Desire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Streetcar\_Named\_Desire "A Streetcar Named Desire")_ (2005), and the [Tony Award for Best Actress in a Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Play "Tony Award for Best Actress in a Play") for _[Doubt: A Parable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doubt:\_A\_Parable "Doubt: A Parable")_ (2024).

For her breakthrough film role as a troubled single mother in the thriller _[Gone Baby Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone\_Baby\_Gone "Gone Baby Gone")_ (2007), Ryan was nominated for the [Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress"). Her other films include _[You Can Count on Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Can\_Count\_on\_Me "You Can Count on Me")_ (2000), _[Capote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capote\_(film) "Capote (film)")_ (2005), _[Before the Devil Knows You're Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Before\_the\_Devil\_Knows\_You're\_Dead "Before the Devil Knows You're Dead")_ (2007), _[Changeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changeling\_(film) "Changeling (film)")_ (2008), _[Birdman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birdman\_(film) "Birdman (film)")_ (2014), _[Bridge of Spies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge\_of\_Spies\_(film) "Bridge of Spies (film)")_ (2015), _[The Infiltrator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Infiltrator\_(2016\_film) "The Infiltrator (2016 film)")_ (2016), _[Beautiful Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beautiful\_Boy\_(2018\_film) "Beautiful Boy (2018 film)")_ (2018), and _[Beau Is Afraid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beau\_Is\_Afraid "Beau Is Afraid")_ (2023).

On television, she played [Beadie Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beadie_Russell "Beadie Russell") in the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") crime series _[The Wire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wire "The Wire")_ (2002–2008) and [Holly Flax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holly_Flax "Holly Flax") in the [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") sitcom _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Office\_(American\_TV\_series) "The Office (American TV series)")_ (2008–2011), and has also featured in the HBO drama series _[In Treatment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In\_Treatment "In Treatment")_ (2010), the [Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulu "Hulu") mystery comedy series _[Only Murders in the Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only\_Murders\_in\_the\_Building "Only Murders in the Building")_ (2021–2024), and the [Apple TV+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_TV+ "Apple TV+") neo-noir mystery series _[Sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar\_(2024\_TV\_series) "Sugar (2024 TV series)")_ (2024).

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Amy_Ryan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Ryan was born Amy Beth Dziewiontkowski in [Flushing, Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flushing,_Queens "Flushing, Queens"), in New York City, the daughter of Pamela (née Ryan),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Ryan#cite_note-wapo-JgB-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Ryan#cite_note-quilts-3) a [nurse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nurse "Nurse"), and John Dziewiontkowski, a trucking business owner. She is of Polish, Irish, and English descent.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Ryan#cite_note-ref310-4) Growing up in the 1970s, Ryan and her sister Laura delivered the _[Daily News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily\_News\_(New\_York) "Daily News (New York)")_ by bike. **X-Factor Investigations** is a fictional detective agency appearing in [American comic books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_comic_book "American comic book") published by [Marvel Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Comics "Marvel Comics"). The organization was created by writer [Peter David](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_David "Peter David") for the [comic book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_book "Comic book") series _[X-Factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Factor\_(comics) "X-Factor (comics)")_ (vol. 3). The agency is made up of [mutant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutant_(Marvel_Comics) "Mutant (Marvel Comics)") heroes operating in [District X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_X "District X"), solving crimes committed by and against mutants.

The team was founded by [Jamie Madrox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Madrox "Jamie Madrox"), and fellow former [X-Factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Factor_(comics) "X-Factor (comics)") members [Strong Guy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strong_Guy "Strong Guy") and [Wolfsbane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolfsbane_(character) "Wolfsbane (character)"). Long-term members later join, including [Siryn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siryn "Siryn"), [M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M_(Marvel_Comics) "M (Marvel Comics)"), [Rictor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rictor "Rictor"), [Shatterstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatterstar "Shatterstar"), and [Layla Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Layla_Miller "Layla Miller"). The team fully disbands with the end of the series, issue #262 (September, 2013).

The agency first appears under the name **XXX Investigations** in the first issue of the Marvel Comics limited series _[Madrox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrox "Madrox")_ #1 (November 2004). In the final issue, _Madrox_ #5 (March 2005), the name is changed to **X-Factor Investigations**, and later abbreviated **XF Investigations**.

X-Factor Investigations is reopened on [Krakoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krakoa "Krakoa") during the [Krakoan Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krakoan_Age "Krakoan Age") of X-Men comics, featured in the [2020 X-Factor title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Factor_(2020_comic_book) "X-Factor (2020 comic book)").

## Publication history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=X-Factor_Investigations&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Publication history")]

Peter David introduced the agency in the limited series _Madrox_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Factor_Investigations#cite_note-Madrox-1) The _Madrox_ series ended in March 2005, but with positive fan and retailer reaction to the book, Marvel relaunched the series under their oft-used title _X-Factor_, David having considered _Madrox_ an _X-Factor_ book anyway.[_[dead link](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Link\_rot "Wikipedia:Link rot")_][[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Factor_Investigations#cite_note-davidint-2) At the 2005 [San Diego Comic Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic-Con_International "Comic-Con International"), David announced the agency would continue, following events in _Madrox_ and _[House of M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House\_of\_M "House of M")_ and intended the agency to be "dark and scruffy," inspired by the [paranormal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paranormal "Paranormal")[Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company") TV series _[X-Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Files "X-Files")_.[_[dead link](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Link\_rot "Wikipedia:Link rot")_][[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Factor_Investigations#cite_note-SDCC-3) At the 2009 Fan Expo Canada, it was announced that the current X-Factor series would be re-numbered to #200 in December 2009, to take up the numbering of the original series.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Factor_Investigations#cite_note-4) The series ended after issue #262, after 114 issues.

## Fictional team history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=X-Factor_Investigations&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Fictional team history")]

**X-Factor Investigations** is a detective agency run by [Jamie Madrox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Madrox "Jamie Madrox"), formerly known as the costumed superhero Multiple Man. The agency was originally named _XXX Investigations_, but team members thought that it sounded too much like Madrox was investigating [pornography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pornography "Pornography"). The new name is taken from the government-sponsored mutant supergroup that the three founders had previously served on.

### "Madrox" and "Decimation"

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=X-Factor_Investigations&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: \"Madrox\" and \"Decimation\"")]

The initial staff consisted of Madrox's best friend and special enforcer, Guido Carosella ([Strong Guy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strong_Guy "Strong Guy")) and former teammate Rahne Sinclair ([Wolfsbane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolfsbane_(character) "Wolfsbane (character)")). Following the [House of M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_M "House of M"), Madrox's newfound wealth from winning a _[Who Wants to Be a Millionaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who\_Wants\_to\_Be\_a\_Millionaire "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire")_-style [game show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_show "Game show") allowed him to recruit several of his former colleagues of the [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris") branch of the now defunct [X-Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Corporation "X-Corporation"). New members include [Siryn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siryn "Siryn"), a powerless [Rictor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rictor "Rictor"), [M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M_(Marvel_Comics) "M (Marvel Comics)"), and [Layla Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Layla_Miller "Layla Miller"), who has inserted herself into the group to keep them from discovering the truth behind the mutant [Decimation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decimation_(comics) "Decimation (comics)"), a catastrophic worldwide wiping out of mutant powers that took place during [a storyline of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decimation_(comics) "Decimation (comics)"). The agency subsequently conflict with rival agency Singularity Investigations, after they ordered Siryn beaten and left for dead.[_[volume and issue needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_]

In the aftermath of the "Decimation" storyline, Madrox, after meeting with Singularity CEO Damian Tryp, asks Siryn to find out more about the Decimation from the heroes who might have been involved. She learns from [Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man "Spider-Man") that the [X-Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Men "X-Men") (who had denied any involvement), as well as [Quicksilver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quicksilver_(Marvel_Comics) "Quicksilver (Marvel Comics)") were, in fact, central to the ending of that event.

In [comic books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_book "Comic book") and other stories with a long history, **first appearance** refers to the first issue to feature a fictional [character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Character_(arts) "Character (arts)"). These issues are often highly valued by collectors due to their rarity and iconic status.

## Reader interest in first appearances

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=First_appearance&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Reader interest in first appearances")]

[Collectors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_book_collecting "Comic book collecting") value first appearances for their rarity and historical value, while many regular readers are interested in viewing how their favorite characters were originally portrayed. Reprints of first appearances are often published, both as single comic books and in [trade paperbacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_paperback_(comics) "Trade paperback (comics)"), usually with other early appearances of the character. [Marvel Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Comics "Marvel Comics")' "Essential" line has become popular by giving readers an affordable glimpse into characters' early history.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_appearance#cite_note-1)

Historically, first appearances tell the [origin story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origin_story "Origin story") for the character, although some, such as [Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman "Batman") and [Green Goblin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Goblin "Green Goblin"), remained dubious figures for several issues. [Modern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Age_of_Comic_Books "Modern Age of Comic Books") writers prefer to tell a character's origin across an entire story arc or keep a newly introduced character mysterious until a "secret origin" issue. Some fans consider this a [gimmick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gimmick "Gimmick") and prefer the older method.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_appearance#cite_note-2)

The artistic merit of many first appearances is debatable. The events portrayed in most famous first appearances are continuously [retconed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retroactive_continuity "Retroactive continuity"), [rebooted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reboot_(fiction) "Reboot (fiction)"), or expanded upon by subsequent writers. Like many [golden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Age_of_Comic_Books "Golden Age of Comic Books") and [silver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Age_of_Comic_Books "Silver Age of Comic Books") age comics, first appearances often become dated and do not fit the modern portrayal of the character.

Some first appearances are considered classics, however. 1990s-era [Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man "Spider-Man") writer [Howard Mackie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Mackie "Howard Mackie") said that his favorite story featuring the character was his first appearance and origin story in _[Amazing Fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazing\_Fantasy "Amazing Fantasy")_ #15 (August 1962), stating that writer [Stan Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Lee "Stan Lee") and artist [Steve Ditko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Ditko "Steve Ditko") "gave us everything we needed, I wanted or could ask for in the least possible space. Every single person who retells the origin never improves on the original, they simply expand it".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_appearance#cite_note-3)

## Monetary value of first appearance issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=First_appearance&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Monetary value of first appearance issues")]

First appearances of popular characters are among the most valuable comic books in existence. Of the "ten most valuable comic books" listed in the spring 2002 issue of _[Overstreet Comic Book Price Guide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overstreet\_Comic\_Book\_Price\_Guide "Overstreet Comic Book Price Guide")_, seven are first appearances of popular [superheroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superhero "Superhero").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_appearance#cite_note-4) Another, _[Marvel Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel\_Mystery\_Comics "Marvel Mystery Comics")_ #1 (October 1939), is the first appearance of the [Golden Age Human Torch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Torch_(android) "Human Torch (android)"), but is more noteworthy as the first comic published by [Marvel Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Comics "Marvel Comics").

It can take many years for a character to attain sufficient popularity after their first appearance to be considered "iconic". By the point a character reaches that level of popularity, it is common for few copies of their first appearance issues to remain. Furthermore, even fewer of those remaining copies will be in the pristine condition prized by collectors. What few remain can be worth thousands of dollars to interested collectors. For example, in 2004, a copy of _[Flash Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flash\_Comics "Flash Comics")_ #1 (January 1940), the first appearance of [The Flash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Garrick "Jay Garrick"), was [auctioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auction "Auction") for $42,000[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_appearance#cite_note-5) and a copy of _Captain America Comics_ #1 (March 1941), the first appearance of [Captain America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_America "Captain America") sold for $64,400.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_appearance#cite_note-6) In 2010, another copy of _Flash Comics_ #1 sold privately for $450,000.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_appearance#cite_note-7)

The first appearance of [Superman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman "Superman"), [_Action Comics_ #1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_Comics_1 "Action Comics 1") (June 1938), has been regarded as the "[holy grail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Grail "Holy Grail")" of comic books due to its cultural significance and rarity; fewer than one hundred copies are thought to exist.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_appearance#cite_note-:0-8) Superman is widely considered to have solidified, if not created, the superhero archetype; therefore, his first appearance is not only important to fans of the character but to fans of superheroes and comic books as a whole.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_appearance#cite_note-9) Well-preserved copies of _Action Comics_ #1 have been sold at auction for record-breaking prices. A copy graded at 8.0 ("very fine") on the 10-point scale typically used by collectors was sold at auction for $1,000,000 in 2010.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_appearance#cite_note-10) Even a copy graded at a much lower 5.5 ("fine minus") sold for $956,000 in 2016.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_appearance#cite_note-:0-8)

Shortly after the record-breaking million-dollar sale of _Action Comics_ #1 in 2010, a copy of _[Detective Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detective\_Comics "Detective Comics")_ #27 featuring the first appearance of [Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman "Batman") was sold for $1,075,000 in a [Heritage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heritage_Auctions "Heritage Auctions") auction.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_appearance#cite_note-11)

Several factors determine the value of a first appearance. All values are according to [ComicsPriceGuide.com](https://web.archive.org/web/20060114071046/http://www.comicspriceguide.com/Default.asp) and are for editions certified by the [Certified Collectibles Group](https://www.cgccomics.com/):

# Top 100 Kenyans 2025: The Full List

*   by [Samuel Mwanawanjuguna](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/by/Mwanawanjuguna) on Thursday, 4 December 2025 - 7:01 am 

![Image 2: A graphic showing sections of Kenyans nominated in Top 100 Kenyans 2025 list by Kenyans.co.ke, December 3, 2025.](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/files/styles/article_style/public/images/media/top-100-site-banner.jpg.webp?itok=75QtdwH5)

A graphic showing sections of Kenyans nominated in the Top 100 Kenyans 2025 list by Kenyans.co.ke, December 3, 2025.

Photo

Alfonce Valerio, Kenyans.co.ke

2025 has been an extraordinary year. Artificial intelligence rattled workplaces, protests reshaped national conversations, and fresh political alignments triggered a feverish run-up to the November by-elections.

Yet amid the unpredictability, a select group of Kenyans didn’t merely weather the turbulence, they defined it. Their influence has earned them a place on the highly regarded and eagerly awaited Top 100 Kenyans 2025.

Marking the eighth edition of this annual project, our newsroom tracked the disruptors, the people who dared to drive change between January and December.

Over the past year, influence in 2025 shifted from traditional power centres to individuals displaying leadership amid disruption and community need. Grassroots problem-solvers, particularly those addressing water scarcity, climate shocks, and economic challenges for youth and SMEs, stepped into focus as first responders and local organisers.

Technology also redefined influence, with AI adoption and fintech gains propelling young technologists and digital advocates to prominence. Creators and homegrown innovators increasingly drove national debates, shaping conversations outside established institutions.

Kenyans Embed URL

Against this backdrop, countless Kenyans stepped up. Some shifted systems, others protected rights, and others rewired entire industries. From this wider pool,[_Kenyans.co.ke_](http://kenyans.co.ke/) refined a lean list of 100 individuals who genuinely stood out.

From marathon legend Eliud Kipchoge to industry titans like Tom Gitogo, the CEO of Britam, and Charlot Magayi, the entrepreneur and climate activist who founded Mukuru Clean Stoves, this year’s Top 100 Kenyans presents some of the people who truly defined 2025 in one way or another.

Identifying them demanded more than tallying headlines or counting followers. It required discipline, scrutiny, and a willingness to challenge comfortable assumptions.

That responsibility fell to the project leads, Brian Muuo, Head of Social Media and Campaigns, and Edwin Kuria, Head of Video and Projects, who steered the review process with a firm insistence on credibility and evidence.

The pair oversaw months of internal debates, fact-checking, and pushback as the newsroom worked to determine who truly moved the needle between January and December.

In order to bulletproof the system, the team introduced a multi-layered verification and audit workflow, where every nomination passed through independent fact-checking teams.

Edwin says these teams were tasked with validating achievements, timelines, affiliations, and real-world impact using publicly available data rather than press releases, sponsored content, or unverifiable claims.

“Second, we implemented a conflict-of-interest declaration system for all reviewers, ensuring that anyone with personal, professional, or organisational ties to a nominee was recused from evaluating that candidate,” he said.

Insisting, “This eliminated the subtle influence that can come from proximity, networks, or institutional loyalty.”

“If a nomination raised even a whisper of external pressure, it was put under a microscope. The final 100 is clean because the process was ruthless,” Brian asserted.

**Edi Mūe Gathegi** ([/ˈ ɛ d i ˈ m w eɪ ɡ ə ˈ θ ɛ ɡ i/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English");[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] born March 10, 1979) is a [Kenyan-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan-American "Kenyan-American") actor. He had his breakthrough playing Dr. Jeffrey "Big Love" Cole on the fourth season of the television series _[House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House\_(TV\_series) "House (TV series)")_ (2007), followed by his roles as Cheese in the 2007 film _[Gone Baby Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone\_Baby\_Gone "Gone Baby Gone")_, vampire [Laurent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Twilight_characters#Laurent "List of Twilight characters") in the films _[Twilight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight\_(2008\_film) "Twilight (2008 film)")_ and its sequel _[The Twilight Saga: New Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Twilight\_Saga:\_New\_Moon "The Twilight Saga: New Moon")_, and as [Darwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darwin_(character) "Darwin (character)") in _[X-Men: First Class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Men:\_First\_Class "X-Men: First Class")_. He played covert operative Matias Solomon on _[The Blacklist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blacklist "The Blacklist"),_ which he reprised for the spinoff series _[The Blacklist: Redemption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blacklist:\_Redemption "The Blacklist: Redemption")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-Spinoff-2)

Gathegi is also featured in the AMC series _[Into the Badlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Into\_the\_Badlands\_(TV\_series) "Into the Badlands (TV series)")_ as Baron Jacobee. He has also played a leading role in _[Startup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/StartUp\_(TV\_series) "StartUp (TV series)")_, a television drama series on [Crackle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crackle_(streaming_service) "Crackle (streaming service)"). Since 2022, Gathegi has played engineer and entrepreneur [Dev Ayesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dev_Ayesa "Dev Ayesa") in the [Apple TV+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_TV+ "Apple TV+") original [science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction_on_television "Science fiction on television") space [drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama "Drama") series _[For All Mankind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For\_All\_Mankind\_(TV\_series) "For All Mankind (TV series)")_, and played [Mister Terrific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mister_Terrific_(Michael_Holt) "Mister Terrific (Michael Holt)") in the [DC Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Universe_(franchise) "DC Universe (franchise)") film _[Superman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman\_(2025\_film) "Superman (2025 film)")_ (2025).

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edi_Gathegi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Born on March 10, 1979,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-3) in [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"), [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), Gathegi grew up in [Albany, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany,_California "Albany, California"), U.S.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-vf-5) Gathegi attended the [University of California, Santa Barbara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Santa_Barbara "University of California, Santa Barbara"), where he played basketball until a knee injury ended his career. Gathegi then began taking acting classes.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-vf-5) He studied at [New York University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University "New York University")'s [Graduate Acting Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tisch_School_of_the_Arts#Graduate_Acting_Program "Tisch School of the Arts") at the [Tisch School of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tisch_School_of_the_Arts "Tisch School of the Arts"), graduating in 2005.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-6) Gathegi's career began in theatre,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-tl1-7) and his stage credits include _[Two Trains Running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two\_Trains\_Running "Two Trains Running")_ at the [Old Globe Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Globe_Theatre "Old Globe Theatre"), _[As You Like It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/As\_You\_Like\_It "As You Like It")_, _[Twelfth Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelfth\_Night "Twelfth Night")_, _[Othello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Othello "Othello")_, _[A Midsummer Night's Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Midsummer\_Night's\_Dream "A Midsummer Night's Dream")_, and _[Cyrano de Bergerac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyrano\_de\_Bergerac\_(play) "Cyrano de Bergerac (play)")_, among others.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-mue-1)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edi_Gathegi&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Gathegi's first professional role was the [Haitian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti") Cabbie in the 2006 film, _[Crank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crank\_(film) "Crank (film)")_. Though he had originally auditioned for the role of Kaylo, the producers gave the role to [Efren Ramirez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efren_Ramirez "Efren Ramirez") and instead offered Gathegi an appearance as the Haitian Cabbie.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-tl1-7) He was skeptical at first about performing a [Haitian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti") accent but was coached by a Haitian friend.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-tl1-7) In 2007, after guest-starring on _[Lincoln Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln\_Heights\_(TV\_series) "Lincoln Heights (TV series)")_ and _[Veronica Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica\_Mars "Veronica Mars")_, Gathegi went on to star as Bodie in _[Death Sentence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death\_Sentence\_(2007\_film) "Death Sentence (2007 film)")_, Darudi in _[The Fifth Patient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fifth\_Patient "The Fifth Patient"),_ and Cheese in _[Gone Baby Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone\_Baby\_Gone "Gone Baby Gone")_. He later had a recurring role as [Mormon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mormonism "Mormonism") intern Dr. Jeffrey Cole in the television medical drama _[House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House\_(TV\_series) "House (TV series)")_. His character was often mocked for his religious beliefs by [Dr. House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregory_House "Gregory House"), who himself is an [atheist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheist "Atheist"). He also guest-starred in _[CSI: Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CSI:\_Miami "CSI: Miami")_, _[CSI: Crime Scene Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CSI:\_Crime\_Scene\_Investigation "CSI: Crime Scene Investigation")_ and _[Life on Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life\_on\_Mars\_(American\_TV\_series) "Life on Mars (American TV series)")_ in 2008 before being cast as Laurent in _[Twilight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight\_(2008\_film) "Twilight (2008 film)")_. When Gathegi first auditioned for the 2008 film, adapted from the same-titled [first book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight_(Meyer_novel) "Twilight (Meyer novel)") in [Stephenie Meyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephenie_Meyer "Stephenie Meyer")'s [Twilight series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight_(novel_series) "Twilight (novel series)"), he had not heard of the series and was not aware that his character was a vampire.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-lat-8) Gathegi later read the whole series and now considers himself a hardcore fan.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-lat-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-9)

He portrayed [Eddie Willers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Willers "Eddie Willers") in _[Atlas Shrugged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlas\_Shrugged\_(film) "Atlas Shrugged (film)")_ (2011), based on [Ayn Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayn_Rand "Ayn Rand")'s [novel of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlas_Shrugged "Atlas Shrugged"). He later portrayed another Haitian character, Jean Baptiste, in the fifth season of _[Justified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justified\_(TV\_series) "Justified (TV series)")_, but was unhappy with the role and asked to be written off the show.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-11) He has also been a recurring character in NBC's television series _[The Blacklist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blacklist "The Blacklist")_ as Matias Solomon, an operative for a covert organization. Gathegi reprised the role in the 2016–2017 season [crime thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_thriller "Crime thriller")_[The Blacklist: Redemption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blacklist:\_Redemption "The Blacklist: Redemption")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-Spinoff-2) He also portrays the character Ronald Dacey on _[StartUp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/StartUp\_(TV\_series) "StartUp (TV series)")_. In July 2025, Gathegi appeared as [Mister Terrific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mister_Terrific_(Michael_Holt) "Mister Terrific (Michael Holt)") in the [DC Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Universe_(franchise) "DC Universe (franchise)") (DCU) film _[Superman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman\_(2025\_film) "Superman (2025 film)")_ (2025).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edi_Gathegi#cite_note-12)

He is married to Adriana Marinescu.

**Efren Antonio Ramírez**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efren_Ramirez#cite_note-2) (born October 2, 1973)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efren_Ramirez#cite_note-Celeb_Bdays-1) is an American actor. He is best known for playing Pedro Sánchez in the 2004 indie film _[Napoleon Dynamite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon\_Dynamite "Napoleon Dynamite")_. He later reprised his role in the [2012 animated series of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon_Dynamite_(TV_series) "Napoleon Dynamite (TV series)").

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Efren_Ramirez&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Ramírez was born on October 2, 1973, in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), to [Salvadoran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvadorans "Salvadorans") parents. He has four brothers, one of whom is his identical twin Carlos.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efren_Ramirez#cite_note-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Efren_Ramirez&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Ramirez has starred in a number of films, including _Napoleon Dynamite_ as Pedro Sánchez, _[Employee of the Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Employee\_of\_the\_Month\_(2006\_film) "Employee of the Month (2006 film)")_, _[Crank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crank\_(film) "Crank (film)")_ and _[Crank: High Voltage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crank:\_High\_Voltage "Crank: High Voltage")_, _Searching for Mickey Fish_, _[All You've Got](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All\_You've\_Got "All You've Got")_, and _[Walkout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkout\_(film) "Walkout (film)")_ and made cameos in _[Nacho Libre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nacho\_Libre "Nacho Libre")_ and _[Mr. & Mrs. Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_&\_Mrs.\_Smith\_(2005\_film) "Mr. & Mrs. Smith (2005 film)")_. In 2011, Efren starred in the comedy _[American Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Summer\_(2008\_film) "American Summer (2008 film)")_ as well as appearing as a contestant on MTV's _[Celebrity Rap Superstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity\_Rap\_Superstar "Celebrity Rap Superstar")_. On July 14, 2008 [Sierra Mist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Mist "Sierra Mist") released a series of commercials aimed at multicultural consumers in which Efren stars.

Soon after the success of _Napoleon Dynamite_, the music group [G. Love and Special Sauce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G._Love_and_Special_Sauce "G. Love and Special Sauce") asked Efren to appear in their music video "Booty Call". He also played [Ashlee Simpson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashlee_Simpson "Ashlee Simpson")'s boyfriend in the music video for her 2005 song "[Boyfriend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boyfriend_(Ashlee_Simpson_song) "Boyfriend (Ashlee Simpson song)")". Ramírez made a cameo appearance in a 2005 episode of [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company")'s _[George López](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George\_Lopez\_(TV\_series) "George Lopez (TV series)")_ wearing a T-shirt similar to the shirt [Jon Heder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Heder "Jon Heder") wears in _Napoleon Dynamite_ that reads, "Vote For Pedro". In 2007 Ramírez appeared as the judge for an acting challenge on [Cycle 8 of _America's Next Top Model_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Next_Top_Model,_Cycle_8 "America's Next Top Model, Cycle 8").

Ramírez made several cameos throughout his career. In [_King Cobra_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Cobra_(1999_film) "King Cobra (1999 film)"), he portrayed a teenager playing a game of [hide-and-seek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hide-and-seek "Hide-and-seek") with his girlfriend (portrayed by Ramirez's wife [Iyari Limon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iyari_Limon "Iyari Limon")). They later end up as prey for the title [antagonist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antagonist "Antagonist"). In the music video for [Sleazy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleazy_(Kesha_song) "Sleazy (Kesha song)"), Pedro appears as a cameo and lip syncs [André 3000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9_3000 "André 3000")'s verse.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efren_Ramirez#cite_note-4)

He co-founded Powerhouse Pictures Entertainment, LLC with [Chris Barrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Barrett_(filmmaker) "Chris Barrett (filmmaker)"), and they co-authored the book _Direct Your Own Life: How To Be A Star in Any Field You Choose_ being published on June 10, 2008 through [Kaplan Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaplan_Publishing "Kaplan Publishing").

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Efren_Ramirez&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

In 1998, Ramírez married actress [Iyari Limon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iyari_Limon "Iyari Limon"). [[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efren_Ramirez#cite_note-6)

Ramírez is also a [DJ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ "DJ"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efren_Ramirez#cite_note-7) who has performed worldwide and toured in over 50 cities across 5 continents. His sets include a variety of music, from [hip hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop "Hip hop"), [funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk "Funk"), [disco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco "Disco"), to [hard house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_house "Hard house"). His production company "Nocturnal Rampage" throws a recurring [rave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rave "Rave") event every summer in [Austin, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin,_Texas "Austin, Texas").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efren_Ramirez#cite_note-yahoo.com-5)

# Meet X-Men Star You Didn't Know Was Kenyan

*   by [Marvin Chege](https://www.kenyans.co.ke/by/marvin) on Monday, 10 February 2020 - 12:00 pm 

Kenya is famous for numerous personalities who have flown the country’s flag high. From athletes like Eliud Kipchoge to football stars like Victor Wanyama to music personalities such as Sauti Sol who have set the entire continent alight with their music.

Little is, however, known of international actors who have made it on the international stage and were born in the country.Lupita Nyong’o the obvious name that comes to mind.The next should be X-Men star Edi Gathegi.

The Kenyan-American actor has been featured in several Hollywood films. He was born in 1979 in Umoja Estate, located in the Eastlands area of Nairobi County. He moved to the United States with his family to the city of Albany in California when he was just three years old.

He went to the University of California in Santa Barbara, California, USA where he played basketball. However, he suffered a knee injury which ended his basketball career.

This setback resulted in him taking acting classes and moving to New York University's Graduate Acting Program at the Tisch School of the Arts in 2002 and graduating in the year 2005.

The following year he scored his first major role, appearing alongside English actor Jason Statham and American actress Amy Smart in the 2006 action film _Crank_. He quickly earned roles alongside Hollywood aces Kevin Bacon in _Sentence_ and as character Cheese in Ben Affleck’s _Gone Baby Gone_.

He was not only gaining success in film, but he also was turning heads on television.

He appeared on _CSI: Miami,_ and earned much recognition and popularity for his recurring role as Dr. Jeffery “Big Love” Cole on _House M.D_. He also got a role in a popular TV show,_The Blacklist Season 3_, Mr. Solomon (Gathegi’s character) acting behalf of The Cabal, an alliance made up of some of the most powerful people in the world.

Other roles include _Kalume Ungara_ in an episode of _Nikita_, _Iggy_ as well as various characters in two episodes of animation series _Phineas and Ferb_ as well as _Jacobee_ in two episodes of _Into the Badlands_.

Gathegi’s career was gaining momentum and he received a suggestion from a casting director about auditioning for a role as a vampire in _The Twilight_ Saga.

He auditioned for the film and landed the role of _Laurent_ in the fantasy film. _Twilight_ became an international success and he retained his role for the franchise’s second film. He earned another high profile role as Armando Muñoz/Darwin in the Marvel Comics superhero film _X-Men: First Class._

Edi loves ugali as well as potatoes and is a fan of the Sauti Sol band. He spends his time travelling, playing sports, reading and watching movies, and prefers to spend his time in New York.

He is currently starring as Ronald Dacey, one of the main characters in the television drama series _StartUp._

Good Morning, get your Monday off to the right start! As we meet Kenyan’s accomplished actor, writer, journalist and television presenter, who’s powerful baritone and mastery of English makes him one of the most recognizable faces and voices in Kenyan radio and television; his no other than John Sibi Okumu!

He has acted in several film productions, among them as the fictional Minister for Health Dr. Joshua Ngaba in the Oscar-winning "The Constant Gardener" and as the real life UN diplomat Jacques Roger Boh-Boh in Shake Hands with the Devil, the story of the Rwanda genocide through the eyes of French-Canadian general Romeo Dallaire. Over the years he has appeared in some 40 lead roles on stage that is Shakespeare in Romeo, Samule Beckett’s Vladimir in Waiting for Godot and Mtwa/Ngema’s Percy in Woza amongst others. He has written two players being Role play – A journey into the Kenyan Psyche (2005) and the second one being Minister…Karibu in 2007 as well as directed the musical Mo Faya shown at the 2009 New York Musical Theatre Festival.

# Making sure you're not a bot!

Loading...

Anubis could not load its JavaScript. The server may be overloaded. Please reload the page to try again.

You are seeing this because the administrator of this website has set up Anubis to protect the server against the scourge of AI companies aggressively scraping websites. This can and does cause downtime for the websites, which makes their resources inaccessible for everyone.

Anubis is a compromise. Anubis uses a Proof-of-Work scheme in the vein of Hashcash, a proposed proof-of-work scheme for reducing email spam. The idea is that at individual scales the additional load is ignorable, but at mass scraper levels it adds up and makes scraping much more expensive.

Ultimately, this is a placeholder solution so that more time can be spent on fingerprinting and identifying headless browsers (EG: via how they do font rendering) so that the challenge proof of work page doesn't need to be presented to users that are much more likely to be legitimate.

Please note that Anubis requires the use of modern JavaScript features that plugins like JShelter will disable. Please disable JShelter or other such plugins for this domain.

End-to-end engineering for teams that need reliable, performant software built to their specifications.

## Frequently Asked Questions

What is Anubis?Anubis is open-source bot protection for the web. It uses proof-of-work challenges to stop automated abuse while letting real users through. It is free, and you host it yourself. Installation instructions are at https://anubis.techaro.lol [link_4].

As we meet Kenyan’s accomplished actor, writer, journalist and television presenter, who’s powerful baritone and mastery of English makes him one of the most recognizable faces and voices in Kenyan radio and television; his no other than John Sibi Okumu!

He has acted in several film productions, among them as the fictional Minister for Health Dr. Joshua Ngaba in the Oscar-winning "The Constant Gardener" and as the real life UN diplomat Jacques Roger Boh-Boh in Shake Hands with the Devil, the story of the Rwanda genocide through the eyes of French-Canadian general Romeo Dallaire. ## What You’ll Find in Our Celebrity Charts

Our pages go beyond simple zodiac signs. We curate a complete profile that blends biographical facts with celestial mechanics.

### 1. Biography & Personal Details

Before diving into the planets, we provide the foundational facts that ground a celebrity’s story:

*   **Summary Bio & Occupation:** A quick snapshot of their journey, from early debuts to current roles (e.g., model, dancer, and singer).
*   **Age & Milestone Tracking:** Real-time age tracking and a countdown to their next birthday.
*   **Family & Relationships:** Key details on siblings, spouses, or children to help you see how their “Moon Sign” (representing home) plays out in real life.
*   **Place of Birth & Education:** Essential context that shapes a celebrity’s early environment.

### 2. Professional Milestones

We list **awards and achievements** to correlate their earthly success with their planetary alignments. When you see a “Grand Prize” win, you can look at the **Transit Analysis** for that year to see if Jupiter (the planet of luck) was making a major move.

### 3. Comprehensive Astrology Analysis

We provide a dual-perspective analysis that is rare in standard horoscopes:

*   **Western (Tropical) vs. Vedic (Sidereal):** See why a star might identify as a Capricorn in the West but a Virgo in the Vedic system.
*   **Numerology Codes:** We calculate Life Path, Birth, and Name numbers to reveal the “vibrational brand” of the celebrity.
*   **Current Cosmic Weather:** Our **Transits Analysis** and **Secondary Progressions** show what the celebrity is experiencing _right now_. For example, a “Saturn opposition Moon” might indicate a period of private emotional growth or a disciplined shift in their public image.

### FAQs

### **Why focus on celebrities?**

Their lives interest many, and Moon-sign charts show how celestial positions might connect to their experiences. Much information is public which is helpful in astrological research and validation of concepts.

### ****What is a Moon-sign birth chart?****

A chart based on the Moon’s position at birth, showing emotions and inner self, as time of birth of most persons is unknown or inaccurate.

### ******How do you determine the “Time of Birth” for these charts?******

Unless a celebrity has publicly shared their exact birth time, we use a default of **12:00 PM UTC (Noon)**. This ensures that planetary positions (like the Sun, Mars, and Jupiter) are accurate for that day, though the Ascendant (Rising Sign) and specific Houses are not calculated to avoid inaccuracies.

### ****What if a celebrity’s birth time is unknown?****

Without exact time, the Moon sign may shift if it changes that day. We use a noon default.

### ****Can I get my own Moon-sign chart here?****

You can apply to get listed in our Birth Chart collection.

### ******How accurate are these interpretations?******

Our birth chart calculations are accurate. However interpretations are subjective to Country, Time and Person, offering insights, not facts.

Each zodiac sign is associated with a specific set of characteristics, strengths, and weaknesses, which are believed to influence an individual’s personality, behavior, and life path.
